name: Name
body:
Across the Tague Bridge, Oriax was coming for their souls.
On Cynthia’s side, the stonework chokepoint over fast-moving waters led only a short distance to the refugee exodus currently fleeing east of Merrin. The harried masses, their children, their tired, and their infirm all lined the highway, desperate to escape the dreaded Orgoth.
A steady stream had been evacuating through the city gates since the day before, and while the procession had been orderly up to now, if Oriax’s advance could not be stopped here, Cynthia knew it would unravel into chaos and mass casualties before nightfall. Already the sun dipped low in the late afternoon of the clear autumn sky. It was yet another dire portent, for nightfall surely favored the Orgoth.
Cynthia understood better than most the horror that came of a soul-devouring invader. The people of Ord were accordingly spooked, their typical defiance fast dissolving as fighting drew closer to Merrin’s outer walls. Cynthia didn’t blame them. They had every reason to be terrified. If they knew even half of what she did, panic would have already taken over.

name: Name
body:
That was why she would cede Oriax not one single inch beyond the Tague, not to her dying breath.
She drew range and stepped center of her formation. With her enemy sighted and closing on the bridge for a third and final time, she shouldered her rune-laden launcher and slapped the receiver shut with a new rune-inscribed rocket inside.
At her back, her father Allister Caine stood with Spellstorms ready, all at once a major, an agent of the CRS, and no less a rogue for all his years. On either side of Caine, his standard squad of elite gun mages formed a firing line like no other. Though the Hellslingers had grown in recent years, the original members of the Black 13th remained foremost at his side, grim-faced and keen-eyed.
At Caine’s right stood the cynic Watts, mutton-chopped and bespectacled, already sighting his long rifle down the no man’s land of the bridge. As he did, the inscribed runes of his barrel flared wanly to his killer instincts and whispered invocations.
To Caine’s left, Ryan crossed the bayonet blades of her magelock dueling pistols, honing their edges with a slow grind. The cruel gleam of her almond eyes narrowed as she marked targets and readied to fight.

name: Name
body:
Alongside Ryan, an age-worn Bastian Falk hefted his scattergun and swore a curse-laden oath to end the first bastards over the barricades. His lined, ruddy skin, hard eyes, and greying beard were no longer the youthful face that had first greeted Cynthia, yet time had done nothing to diminish the zeal in his smile.
Alongside Watts, Corporal Glover cast aside his cloak, tilting back his tricorn with an easy smile and training his magelock downrange as if for sport. The barrel glowed cherry red as his own budding gift of magic began to manifest.
Behind Caine and towering over all the Hellslingers, his warjack Deuce crackled with voltaic power, leveling the sights of a fearsome long-barreled dual cannon in careful anticipation. Like those of the gun mages he protected, Deuce’s barrels were inscribed with a series of runes that began to glow as a firing solution formed within its cortex.
Cynthia’s own warjack Pokey stepped to her side, unmistakably eager to continue killing. As the invaders continued to resupply the battle from on high, her warjack had been continuously reloaded and refitted with new weapons. His guns fully reloaded, he now wore  a high-caliber cannon at his shoulder. Cynthia couldn’t help but sense the excitement coursing through the conduits of her warjack’s artificed mind, as their bond sent it spilling over into her own thoughts. Truly, this was what he was made for.

name: Name
body:
Cynthia’s last defenders spread out before the Hellslingers, three understrength squads lying prone behind makeshift barricades of earth and timber. Just over half the platoon was all that remained after two brutal assault waves—nineteen survivors remained versus eleven dead in a fight where she could not afford to spare a single soul. Yet so long as their invaders kept them supplied, she knew they would hold the line to the last.
She glanced up at The Furious Finn and Cracker Barrel as they circled overhead, and she whispered a prayer to keep them safe. They were mere outlines to her now, held at a standard drop altitude of eight thousand feet. Though it kept their guns well out of range, with the ever-present threat of rhok harriers nearby, there they would stay.
As the final Orgoth wave began to march on their position, she was satisfied that if her Gravediggers should find themselves outnumbered, with the Hellslingers by her side at least they would not be outgunned. Would it be enough?

name: Name
body: They were all about to find out.

name: Name
body:
Behind Oriax’s steady advance, his cursed horde followed, howling their bloodlust in anticipation. Alarmingly, the rising din served to draw in still more combatants—a swarm of the dreaded shapes of leather-winged rhok harriers took to the skies. Cynthia counted a dozen, maybe more, rising from a tree line across the river. Only a hundred yards distant, the wide circles of their rising flight turned for the bridge and Oriax. They shrieked their horrible call on approach, grating screams that struck her nerves worse than any other sound.
Behind an oncoming Gharlghast, Cynthia could see Oriax’s final assault wave was comprised of  four parts: a phalanx of twenty-odd assault reavers each carrying long, hooked pikes at their shoulders; behind them, a half-dozen siege tarasks; then a dozen ulkor gnashers, great red brutes in fearsome masks and light armor gripping axes and blades. Finally, a large mass of skirmishers brought up the rear with all manner of weapons. If she knew her foe, these were meant to overrun the battle and hunt refugees at the first chance. she estimated she saw at least forty of these axe-wielding lunatics.

name: Name
body:
With rhoks suddenly joining the fight and a Gharlghast already on deck, she  felt her heart begin to pound. If not for the Hellslingers and the chokepoint of the Tague Bridge, she knew beyond a doubt there would be no stopping it.
Oriax surely knew this, too.
The Orgoth warlord exuded both menace and mystery as he walked, his face hidden under a polished metal mask and a darkened cowl. His footfalls were deliberate and heavily shod. His long black cloak flapped in the wind, causing a collection of soul cages to jangle with each step from the ends of their chains. He walked straight to the bridge, his hooded gaze never leaving Cynthia.
At the threshold of the crossing, Oriax halted, raising an arm. The titanic Gharlghast reacted to the gesture by stopping behind him, obedient, shifting and stamping its feet with impatience. The Ulkor handlers at its corners unleashed their beast, releasing its chains and lowering their pikes.
Freed, the massive creature stepped forward, hunched down, and dropped to all fours. The crude bladed battering ram it wore for a helm was aimed the length of the bridge, its iron-shod knuckles gashing the earth as the rocket batteries on its back tilted upward.

name: Name
body:
"Ready," Cynthia warned the platoon, tensing for the incoming barrage.
The Gharlghast roared, spittle spilling from the corners of its fanged maw. The Gravediggers hunkered down. When Oriax’s arm dropped, pointing, the rhoks followed his gesture, coming about to fly down the length of the bridge in a tight formation. He guided them as a screen now, giving cover to his precious warbeast as it readied itself to fight.
As the rhoks came screaming in, the Gharlghast braced itself on all fours and shuddered, causing both of its shoulder rocket batteries to fire simultaneously. The spectacular barrage arced high and whistled inbound. One by one, rocket impacts traced a firestorm across the line. They struck the Gravedigger earthworks, blasting them apart and casting up a shower of dirt. Three grunts took shrapnel; all were driven deep into what remained of their cover.
Then the rhok swarm was upon them, shrieking for prey. The huddled Gravediggers were trapped as the rhoks’ claws raked past, shredding their backs as the beasts went by. One trooper, caught by the steely talons by the scruff of his webbing, was immediately dragged skyward, screaming from his cover.

name: Name
body:
Behind the rhoks, the Gharlghast recovered its artillery strike with a howl and followed up by launching itself into a charge. The ferocity of its bounding gait left no doubt that it meant to finish with its iron-shod fists what it had started with its rockets.
Oriax’s opening moves were easy enough to grasp, in Cynthia’s estimation. The rhok swarm was a diversion—if the Gharlghast could crash their fragile line, there would be no recovery for what came next. The battle would soon devolve into a mindless swirl of melee that would ensure an easy Orgoth victory.
Cynthia nodded to herself; the play was as straightforward as it was brutal.
Even so, Oriax had not been expecting fire support from the Hellslingers. She frowned at the Orgoth warlord, who was still waiting on the far side of the bridge. Why did he not come? She observed his command as the assault reavers approached the starting line. He did not appear ready to answer her challenge. But it was a mystery that would have to wait: the rhoks were upon them.

name: Name
body:
"Fire at will," Cynthia commanded, dropping to one knee to take her first shot. Her rocket streaked swiftly, targeting the lead rhok within the swarm.
Behind her rocket, the Hellslingers erupted. It was a firing line like no other, with thunderous blasts of spectral red, green, and blue that tore into the advancing flyers with arcane fury and dazzling pyrotechnics. Their opening volley proved as timely as it was lethal, as the kidnapped Gravedigger found himself quickly dropped to safety.
The offending rhok had little choice—it had been gutted by five bullseyes from Watts, Ryan, and Caine. The carcass hurtled to the ground, leaving a bloody trail on impact. The rescued Gravedigger got to his feet, amazed by his luck; around him, his fellow soldiers cheered at the save and rose up from their cover, returning fire with a vengeance.
"Gravediggers never surrender!" Cynthia cheered and sent a rocket into an oncoming rhok. She blinked from the close blast, feeling the heat on her face as it sent her target bloody, burning, and half-exploded to the earth behind her.

name: Name
body:
Her resurgent soldiers swarmed each fallen, driving at the wounded beasts with bayonet strikes and point-blank fire.
Seeing the inbound Gharlghast behind them, Cynthia wasted no time and loaded another rocket.
"Yeh see him?" She glanced back at her father while Pokey sprayed fire overhead.
"Aye." Caine nodded, his eyes locked to the oncoming Gharlghast even as his Spellstorms blazed away at the rhoks. The rampaging giant was now moving at a full gallop across the bridge, the distance between them reduced to forty yards and closing. "Yeh got a plan?"
"We need to clear the screen first." Cynthia slapped shut her receiver, ready to fire.
"Yeh heard the captain, Hellslingers!" Caine shouted down the line while firing both Spellstorms at an incoming rhok. It sailed over him and then past him; the dead target landed in a rag doll’s roll as if to make his point. "Just like that."
"Yeh and yer pistols," Cynthia smirked, lining her next target high. She squeezed the trigger, forming spectral runes at the muzzle. Her rocket’s flight caught a rhok in its midriff. The spectral blast then caught another of the beasts as it raced past, reducing both creatures to charred meat. Their death showered a sloppy mess over the Gravedigger position, but the soldiers cheered it on just the same. "They’re holding yeh back, old man."

name: Name
body:
"Never mind the kid and her delusions, Deuce." Caine smiled, finding a gap in the flyer screen for a pair of shots on the Gharlghast. Both headshots deflected off the creature’s armored helmet. Caine frowned. "Just focus on the beastie."
Deuce nodded, holding fire for a gap in the screen.
"Steady," Caine urged his warjack, lending it focus as he reloaded his Spellstorms. He squinted, seeing an opening at last. "Have at it."
Deuce leaned in, the double-tap of its weapon like twin hammers to an anvil. The paired shots pressed the gap to strike dead-center of the creature’s chest. The blazing impact struck an ugly gouge in the armor, but the plate held. The monster grunted at the shot, losing no more than a step, with a shake of its armored head. Then Watts followed up with a low blow, striking the Gharlghast’s shin with a luminous blast. The creature grunted again, staggered back another step. Blood leaked from the wound in the creature’s thick, grey flesh.
Cynthia saw the blood spurt, saw the limp. Then the rhok screen loomed again, forcing her down. They needed to keep hitting it, and time was running out. Worse, she needed cover fire. At her side, Pokey and Ryan were busy keeping rhoks clear of the flanks, trading arcs of fire with one another as if born to it. There would be no help there.

name: Name
body:
"I’ve got you, Captain." True to his word, Falk had her back.
The grizzled gun-mage stepped past her with an enthusiastic snarl, blasting an approaching pair of rhoks clear with streaks of burning indigo from his scattergun. Both beasts were engulfed by his arcane blast, shrieking in pain and wheeling away.
"Nice shot." Cynthia slapped her receiver shut and squinted downrange. She winced to see the Gharlghast had gained precious yards despite its limp. Oriax’s screen was working. Another rhok surged in as Falk reloaded, its shadow falling over them both, talons outstretched. Beside him, Glover saw the movement in his periphery and turned to intervene, putting a spell-shot deep in the flyer’s belly.
The rhok’s screeching reply was a retch of a death cry, yet the thing had some fight left still. Its talons nearly had Falk, but the muzzle of his reloaded weapon found its beaked face first. The blast was fatal, his spellfire burst splitting the creature’s head open like a rotten melon.
"Fek me," Falk swore, a victim of his own success. Cynthia saw him fall beside her, lost beneath the rhok’s shuddering leathery wings.

name: Name
body:
"A little old for wrestling aren’t we, Captain?" an amused Glover quipped, dropping to a knee to help free his stricken squadmate from the carcass.
"Are you kidding me?" Falk erupted from under the creature’s wing with a tearing stroke of his blade. He stood, kicking the deceased rhok in the ribs for good measure before sheathing his blade. "I’m not even breaking a sweat here."
"Clear that screen, Hellslingers." Caine refocused his frenetic firing line. "Gharlghast coming in fast!"
As rune shots and rifle fire at last drove the diminished rhoks back, a final opening presented itself. Cynthia found her target at thirty yards; its massive footfalls shook the earth under her feet. It plowed through the ruined earthworks, coming straight for her, taking fire on all sides from the Gravediggers with little care. It wanted her, she sensed. Cynthia winced, gathering her focus to fire—

name: Name
body:
"Wait." Caine was in her ear, shouting over the gunfire. "I’m gonna set yeh up."
"Yeh better hurry," Cynthia warned, squinting to keep her iron sights on target.
"Hey, it’s me." Caine shrugged, focusing on Deuce. He closed his eyes, empowering his warjack. Under his keen eye, the dual cannon aligned on the crashing Gharlghast, dipping low for the wounded leg…
Deuce double-tapped.
From the warjack’s cannons, a pair of arcane rounds screamed downrange with a vengeance. Both shots exploded into the Gharlghast’s weakened leg, blasting its shin apart in a gory spray. In agony, the creature spilled forward, tumbling down face first and howling its pain.
Alongside Cynthia, Caine seized the moment, launching himself at the fallen Gharlghast with three steps into a run and then into a leap. And then he was gone, lost to the void and reappearing, fully turned around, standing atop the fallen titan’s shoulders.
Caine fired a vicious volley into the back of the creature’s helmeted head and armored collar. Over and again, he blasted at the clasps keeping the creature’s visor affixed, finding resistance still. Moreover, the thing now fought to get him off—and it was winning.

name: Name
body:
"Break damn yeh," Caine swore, knocked off-balance, guns empty. Yet as he fell to the ground, Cynthia saw a link of broken fastening fall with him.  A split second before his arse hit the ground, Caine vanished back into the void.
The struggling beast’s visor dropped sideways, revealing a morbid mass of scarred flesh, surgically exposed teeth, and hideous, unblinking fish-eyes. As its loosened visor tumbled to the ground, the monster looked up with something like desperation in those horrible eyes to see Cynthia aiming at it from twenty yards away.
She did not waste the opening. She squeezed her trigger. Beyond the incandescent runes that haloed her launch tube, a fiery rocket trail streaked for the creature’s exposed face. Then, a dazzling explosion of blue-green arcane sparks unmade its head. As the smoke settled, she saw nothing remained but a ragged stump, pumping blood onto the dirt. At last, the Gharlghast fell over and lay still.
"Nice shot." Caine was beside her again, on his back, breathing hard and reloading his Spellstorms.

name: Name
body:
"Nice set-up." Cynthia exhaled, blinking as she watched the massive creature’s twitching finally cease. Even as the Gravediggers’ cheers went up around her, she looked across the bridge, knowing the battle was a long way from won. With Oriax still to come, the worst was yet to come.
Cynthia stood grim-faced, watching the Reavers ready themselves beyond Gharlghast's carcass to receive their master's signal. The siege tarasks, the gnashers, the skirmishers, all were now stamping with impatience.
And still, Oriax did not come.
Cynthia blinked as she stood up, puzzled to find the Orgoth warlord still shirking her challenge from the far side of the bridge. In fact, all of the Orgoth seemed to pause suddenly as a scout rider approached Oriax on a galloping black steed.
"What’s going on here?" Cynthia pointed, watching as Oriax spoke with the scout.
"If I was a betting man," Caine looked on, holstering his Spellstorms, "I’d say Oriax is after the same thing as SKS-6."
"Who?" Cynthia took a breath, looking at her father with growing suspicion.

name: Name
body: "It’s no accident you’re tied up here." Caine turned to her. "Section 3 sent their best goons under command of one Kapitan Zahara Vilkul." "Khador?" Cynthia shook her head. "Borisyuk would never—" "Probably not." Caine shrugged. "But he ain’t the only one laid eyes on our prize, now was he?" "No." Cynthia sighed. "There was an ex-greylord with him. I didn’t like the look of her, but—do yeh really think they’d stab us in the back over it?" "Old habits die hard, kid. Section 3 wants Orgoth tech, any way they can get it. We’re here to make sure that doesn’t happen." "So, that’s why yer here." Old grudges flared up with the break in the action. She fought to keep it together with a cough. "I mean, we haven’t even spoken in two years. Yeh could have been dead, for all I knew." "That’s how the CRS works, Captain." Caine’s humor fell away quickly. "Maybe yeh remember the deal I made?" "Oh, I remember, Major." Cynthia smiled bitterly. She tried hard to stay focused, but memories of his snub of her battle school graduation in Caspia came flooding back. The last time she had seen him, they had fought about her going at all. There were things said that should not have been. "It’s fine."

name: Name
body:
"We can talk later. There’s more to say." Caine looked across the bridge. "Let’s start with the artifact. Yeh need to tell me where it is, ’cause I reckon that’s where SKS-6 is already headed and where our mutual chum Oriax is about to go."
"How?" Cynthia looked downrange, past the paused reavers and the gnashers and the raiders. Clearly, the scout had Oriax’s full attention. "I had it moved from the ruins."
"Vilkul’s a right fox. She’ll figure out yer little ploy. That one over there can probably just sense it."
"Figures. It was overpowering just to be around."
"Sounds about right." Caine watched Oriax.
"That bad?"
"We actually have no idea. But if both SKS-6 and Oriax want it this much, it pretty much has to be," Caine’s expression was pained.
As Caine and Cynthia watched, Oriax pulled his scout from his mount, throwing the man helplessly to the ground. Oriax then pulled himself into the saddle and abruptly brought the horse about. He brought an arm up and his forces swelled to readiness.
"Guess he’s on his way," Caine said. "Not good."

name: Name
body:
Oriax gestured to the siege tarask riders, his arm circling for them to follow. Then he pointed to the column waiting on the bridge, indicating Cynthia with finality. The reavers answered the call, their front-rank bringing their jagged spears down as they began a solemn march for no man’s land.
With the Orgoth attack officially resumed, Oriax spurred his mount and his new retinue to withdraw from the battle. He led the way at a gallop down the riverbank. Cynthia knew at once they were headed for the ruins.
"No, not good at all," she agreed, recalling the distress flare her Gravediggers had sent up. "They already took the ruins."
Caine watched Oriax go. "Tell me yeh didn’t bring it inside the city."
"Do yeh think I’m stupid?" Cynthia felt her face warm with sudden anger. "Of course I didn’t."
"Yeh were ordered to fly it out first chance, Captain. For a damn good reason." Caine turned to her. "So mind yeh don’t sass me now."
"If I had followed orders, Major," Cynthia bristled, "the refugees just down the road from here would all be dead now."

name: Name
body:
"I ain’t saying you did wrong, kid. I’m just here to make things right. Where did yeh stash it?"
"I had it moved to the field supply depot for safekeeping, south of the city." Cynthia took a breath as the marching enemy grew closer, their pace quickening and their shouts began. "It’s in a plain crate marked for Point Bourne. The only one like it."
"So be it." Caine looked between Cynthia, her circling skyships high overhead and the approaching Orgoth army, brooding.
"What?" Cynthia asked.
"Stay here. Save yer refugees, Captain." Caine jaw set with that familiar look of resolve. "The Hellslingers are on the job now."
"What are yeh going to do?"
"If Oriax is moving for the depot," Caine said as he turned toward the low-hanging sunset, "we’ll get there first."
"Well, good luck, Major." Cynthia watched him go as the enemy came on.

name: Name
body: "We have to go back, Lieutenant." Chief engineer Morse shook his head, the windy deck unraveling the grey wisps of his carefully managed comb-over. "We can’t stay here." At the prow of the Cloudpiercer amidst the humid night winds, Bastion Falk turned at the engineer’s approach. He studied the pot-bellied Cygnaran with narrowing eyes and a hand covering his holstered weapon, wary of some ploy. For his part, the veteran engineer tugged the straps of his worn denim overalls yet was careful to avoid eye contact. Instead, his attention followed Falk’s hand. "We can’t." Falk exhaled and turned to look out over the open deck of the Cloudpiercer. The cover of their low-hanging cloud was thinning out as it spilled over the deck with tendrils of damp mist. Even at this altitude, the stink of sulfur was in his nose, inescapable. A piece at a time, Skell was revealed far below. For the moment at least, what he most wanted to see was not yet visible. "The skydrive don’t care much what’s down there." Morse swallowed, his eyes slowly meeting Falk’s. "The boilers are dry at four hours’ cruise time no matter if we fly over friend or foe. Besides which, without cloud cover, every foe will have eyes on us soon enough."

name: Name
body:
"I know it, Morse."  Falk nodded. "Just a little longer is all I ask. This is the extraction point; this is the time we set. They aren’t going home if we leave."
"Hell of a thing, Lieutenant, taking us at gunpoint with a caper such as this. All the way to Skell, no less. If I wasn’t looking at it with my own eyes, I’d never have believed it."
"I am sorry. Like I said, I’ll tell the tribunal you never had a choice. This is on me."
"Only right that you do." Morse looked down. "But the lads and I are in for a penny, in for a pound now."
"Do you have any children of your own, Chief?" Falk turned away from the rail, taking up his spyglass from his belt.
"A pair of girls, aye," The chief said.
"And would you want them down there?" Falk scanned down over the city with his spyglass as he spoke, looking for some trace of Caine.
"No more than your captain does." Morse’s his weathered features hardening. He joined Falk at the rail and peered down at the city.
"He’ll make it." Falk looked at Morse, unsure who needed convincing. "He just needs more time."

name: Name
body:
"I’ll do what I can," Morse said. "Trim the gain. Maybe find some more ballast to jettison. I do suggest you hold us to what cloud cover we have meantime."
"Yes. All right." Falk paced, looking down over the city of Skell as their cloud finally broke completely. Far though it was, he could see green flares of light, towers, temples, and dark shadows in every direction.
He had to be ready for the signal. Yet who was looking back up at them? How long before they sent flyers up to intercept? He could only hope Caine had found his girl by now. Morse wasn’t bluffing.
"Where are you, Allister?" Falk held his breath and focused his spyglass a little farther down the streets of Skell.
Surely, Caine was there, just around the next corner…
***

name: Name
body:
"Allister?" Anastasia peered around the corner, distraught. The Llaelese assassin had ventured up to the end of the alley to find a well-lit boulevard adjacent to their position. "You need to look at this."
"Tell me you see the rally point." Caine shuffled through the alley’s shadows after her with a labored grunt, an exhausted Cynthia carried in the crook of his left arm.
"Oh I see it." Anastasia squinted over a wide scan of the area, her voice notably displeased. "That’s maybe half the battle here."
Behind them, the Hellslingers followed. The pace had been breathless since plucking Cynthia from a fatal fall with Deneghra at large. There was no choice in the matter; every corner they turned now crawled with enemies  assigned at the warwitch’s command. If Skell had seemed a dormant metropolis coming in, it was now very much awake.
Time was not on their side, either. Even now, Falk would be over the extraction point, waiting for a signal flare, as they had agreed. But he could only wait so long before fuel reserves would force them to retreat. Caine very much doubted they could hold out for his gun-mage-turned-ship’s captain to make another pass should that happen.

name: Name
body: What was more, Caine now saw the chilling coordination that came of the walking dead in their own domain. Mechanithralls beyond counting spilled from endless doorways around them, many wielding monstrous iron gauntlets that crackled with power as they marched in mobs. Entire detachments of bane knights had been summoned to join the hunt, their formations marching out from garrison and stationhouses alike along the way. Caine marked skarlock commanders presiding over the file lines and columns. Each of the spectral officers pressed their charges to the hunt in unnerving silence. Oh yes, Caine thought. The jig is definitely up here. As he came alongside Anastasia, he sensed a welling threat before them, something coming in with the force of a geyser. Whatever it was, it was big, fast, and loud. "Take cover," Caine hissed, his eyes wide, and ducked for shadow. Horrible screeching and the rush of foul wind spilled down the boulevard, carried on tattered wings. The murderous murmur of carrion thralls dispersed along the boulevard, passing them by to divide over the canals. With his back to the wall, Caine held his breath at the smell; he kept a hand covering Cynthia’s head, pressing her close. The Hellslingers meanwhile held their place in the shadows with eyes agleam and weapons ready until the danger passed.

name: Name
body:
"A miserable lot, those," Ryan groused. "More than a bandolier can kill, and headshots count for nothing."
Even as the airborne threat passed over, Caine felt the path to freedom narrowing just the same. They had already been forced from their chosen route, skirting around to get back on course through the many quays that serviced the river. The area was a treacherous maze of deep-cut canals built with sheer stone sides. At intervals, enormous, encrusted pipes hung over the canals, spewing green sludge into the murky waters below. AS toxic as the water looked, dark shapes moved under the surface, sometimes breaching with a bony fin or a glimpse of scaly hide that then vanished in the deep.
"Where is the rally point?" Caine risked another look beyond the alley as the last of the carrion thralls departed.
"Over there." Anastasia pointed past the boulevard with one hand. Caine noted she had been favoring her right since their last street scuffle at the gates of the warwitch temple. By now, the Hellslingers were altogether battered, tired and saltier than usual. He had also noticed Bailoch trying to hide a limp. Cynthia, too, had grown pale against his shoulder, her gaze aimless.

name: Name
body:
Yet they were close.
Following Anastasia’s gesture, Caine saw an old factory standing tall in the distance, eight stories tall and easily spotted over the flat expanse of quays and waterways. But the route would expose them to the likes of the carrion flocks—or worse. Caine traced a beeline for the factory beyond and saw little besides crates or scattered barrels they could use for cover. They couldn’t risk a swim, either. Was it a dead end?
A thought intruded, not of his own making.
It was Ace.
"What is it, chum?" Caine turned to find the ’jack stepping alongside, radiating insistence. Ace knelt, craning his mechanical head around and into arm’s reach. Caine knew the offering for what it was, placing his hand there.
Through the warm steel of Ace’s visor, a particular vision formed in Caine’s mind, drawn by Ace from the great reservoirs of the warjack’s cortex memory. Ace had seen a drawbridge across the quays, leading directly to their evacuation point. Caine recognized the captured memory; his warjack had been forced to take an alternate route to exit the scrapyard where they had landed.

name: Name
body:
Caine focused his eyes over the quays in a western direction as Ace suggested. Sure enough, he could make out a faint silhouette through the pall of the dank mist that hung over the fetid waters.
It was the drawbridge.
"For a rust-bucket of a scoundrel, yeh do have yer moments, chum." Caine winked at Ace then turned to his crew. "We have a route."
Ace shrugged off the jab, flipping his chin out of Caine’s touch with mischief as he rose back to a standing pose. He gave an amiable chirp of steam and leaned forward, signaling his readiness to depart.
"None too soon, either," Watts affirmed with urgency at the rearguard of their party. His spectacled eyes marked the advance of the ubiquitous walking dead into their alley. He held his rifle, hesitant to fire until forced to do so. "It crawls here."
"Stay close." Caine ran out into the boulevard, a single Spellstorm covering the way as he led for the promontory’s end at the quays. "I reckon a few jumps to cross this mess."
"Ech." Bailoch spat into the water as he padded after Caine. "I could do without those for a while when we’re finished here."

name: Name
body:
"It can have that effect." Caine waited as they encircled him, looking down at Cynthia to catch the wander of her eyes for a moment. "How about yeh, kid?"
"I don’t feel so good." She was already pale and still losing color.
"Hang in there, darlin’." Caine opened the void. Through his portal, the Hellslingers found themselves relocated to an island platform, ringed by bollards and stacked with haphazard crates ready to be shipped. As they arrived, Caine saw movement through the tangle of the crates: The workforce of mechanithralls assigned to the island were realizing there were intruders among them.
"Have at it!" Caine fired, picking off the first thrall to approach. Behind him, the Hellslingers provided covering fire, advancing.
As Caine fired over and past her, Cynthia blinked, looking up to him with a welling panic. "I really don’t feel so good."
"Give me a second." Caine continued to fire as they walked.
She didn’t have the second to give—she heaved. Once, twice, she retched over and on his shoulder. The mess was black, oily.

name: Name
body:
Caine looked at his soiled shoulder with a grimace. "What they been feeding yeh?"
"I ate a soul." Cynthia sobbed as she said it, wiping her mouth and putting her head back against his chest.
"Yeh did what?" Caine did not stop to reload; he simply kept walking through the crates for the far side of their platform.
"I ate a soul," Cynthia repeated, muffled in his shoulder and sobbing still.
"You ate a soul?" Caine blasted a thrall five paces away while Watts and Ryan covered him from either side in a walking firing line. Within the short canyon of crates, a shooting gallery unfolded as thralls continued to pile in.
"It wasn’t my fault." Cynthia paused as Caine gunned down a thrall within arm’s reach. "At first they tried to make me eat this girl’s soul, and I wouldn’t. I wouldn’t do it!"
"It’s all right." Caine kept firing as they walked. "Then what happened?"
"I could, talk to her, in her cage-thing, yeh know?" The walking dead erupted between crates only to be felled over and over again all around them. "Her name was Elise. Can yeh believe such a thing?"

name: Name
body:
"That’s my girl." Caine reloaded, pausing to look around the corner, glimpsing an open dock and the drawbridge beyond. "Clairvoyance at such a young age."
Cynthia looked up at him, eyes welling even as color came back to her cheeks.
"Then what?" He smiled at her as he shot down a pair of thralls coming from the dock just ahead. Watts and Ryan walked alongside him, keeping pace while matching him kill for kill.
"Then they caught me. The witches." Cynthia paused as Caine pulled them across the canal in a single leap, appearing atop a pier on the other side. The island dock was connected to the quays by two wide attachments.
"Were they ugly witches?" Caine noted columns of bane knights marching for each dock, weapons drawn.
"I don’t know what they were." Cynthia paused, wrinkling her nose as she looked at the bane knights. "They were like sisters but entirely metal at the same time. And they were sneaky. Elise helped me escape, but they caught us. I wasn’t strong enough to fight them, so Elise helped me. It was the only way. She begged me to do it, and I didn’t know what else to do. Deneghra said I’ll never be normal again because of what I’ve done."

name: Name
body:
Again, Cynthia was sobbing, her head down.
"Survival can get ugly, kid." Caine ran the length of their dock, finding another crossing point over the canal. "I reckon Elise was a true friend to do yeh like that. Now dry yer eyes and make what she did count. That’s all there is for it now."
"I can try." Cynthia sniffled, suddenly aware of something she forgot. "Pa!"
"What?" Caine pulled the void open again to sweep the Hellslingers over the canal before them.
"I almost forgot. I found the shadow place," Cynthia proclaimed as they reappeared on the quay.
"The shadow place?" Caine paused to reorient, frustrated. Sure, the drawbridge was only fifty yards now. Maybe two jumps. But he saw the road it serviced ahead was lined with bane knights on approach.
"Just like you," Cynthia said. "That’s how I got away."
"Darlin’, yeh make me proud." Caine hugged his daughter before looking back to the bane knights sealing up the way ahead. "Yeh reckon yeh can walk for me now? I could sure use another gun."
"I think it’s broken." Cynthia nodded at her left leg. "When she made the helljack grab me."

name: Name
body:
"Okay, then. Don’t yeh worry. We’ll just sort these folks out together."
"If yeh say so." She looked ahead to the phalanx of bane knights. As they took their places, each snapped their weapons down to readiness.
Caine inhaled, reloading as he looked back at the rest of his squad.
"I’ll run the middle," Caine said, gathering himself. "Give me some room."
Watts and Ryan traded wry smiles, knowing what came next.
***

name: Name
body: "It’s always Caine!" Deneghra raged, her spear swung round to send the nearest of her thralls off the skybridge as she crossed. The reanimated corpse made the fatal plunge in silence, disintegrating on impact four stories down. But such was the warwitch’s anger that she could scarcely perceive what had just happened, replaying it over and over again in her thoughts. Deneghra’s trusted soul harvesters, Sekka and Lynek, had been destroyed, all but obliterated by Cynthia’s blossoming gift. A blessing it was, too. The girl had proven everything Deneghra could have hoped for. The girl would be forged into a powerful weapon in Toruk’s name. What’s more, Cynthia had been on the very verge of submission. It was all in hand. Or so it seemed. Then the little urchin got free again. Indeed, it seemed her knack. She had gone so far as to compel a helljack to her aid this time. The audacity. When Deneghra had been forced to counter the girl by wresting control away, Cynthia had wriggled free yet again. Then Caine was there. And now both were gone.

name: Name
body:
How?
It boggled Deneghra’s mind, as twisted a turn as she had ever seen. Cygnar’s loosest cannon had somehow come for his daughter, here in the Dragonfather’s heart of darkness. More than that, he had found her and snatched her up right out from under Toruk’s nose. Deneghra seethed with every step that this had happened at all, let alone how it would look. Her simmering rage broke free of her lifeless features at increasing intervals, manifesting as flashes of poisonous green-hued arcane power, her very footsteps crackling over the obsidian floor as she walked.
The temple’s eldest crone and keeper of the witches’ hearth, Aaras Silaa, stood waiting for Deneghra at the temple’s grand entrance. She was clad in scarlet robes and wore her chain of office at her neck. Her fear was plain on the features of her cold dead face.
"Deneghra," Silaa croaked, her fish-belly complexion further paled by Deneghra’s withering glare. "Scopulus has ordered all of Skell’s garrison in pursuit as you demand. We will find them."

name: Name
body:
"You have much to account for, Aaras." Deneghra continued walking, forcing the withered crone to follow along in a scramble. In the air over the city, a familiar presence was arriving, growing closer with each flap of great canvas-wrapped wings. She wagged a finger as the two of them moved for the doors. "The girl ran loose on your watch. I am forced now to get her back."
"Many apologies." Silaa deferred with a bow then followed her mistress through the great double doors of the temple. "What of the wraith?"
"What of it?" Deneghra stopped short on the steps, looking up at the night sky now. He was coming fast, getting closer. She felt their connection surge, his obedience total.
"The wraith is yet loose and the cause of much havoc in our lower levels still.," Silaa admitted, her head low. "Should I divert some of our sisters to defeat it?"
"No. The girl is the only priority now. I will deal with the wraith myself when we have her back."
Silaa raised her hands, looking up from her bow. "I could—"

name: Name
body:
Deneghra felt her anger boil over; Silaa’s groveling had become more than she could bear. She reached up, seizing control of the impending presence overhead. In her mind’s eye, she saw the world from on high, felt the rush of flight in her veins. She was using his sightless vision, and now she sensed prey. Silaa was there below, only a few steps away from her own body. She dove now, wings pointed down, their clawed tips reaching out by her will.
"You could be gone," Deneghra spoke, even as she crashed to earth in control of the great neckromechanikal abomination, a hideous beast of decay held in the grip of the undying arts.
Deneghra’s monstrous mount shook the ground on landing, giving an undulating cry that rasped like fall leaves. Beneath the claws of its wings, Silaa lay crushed, reduced to a smear of pulp and ichor on the steps of the temple.
Deneghra then compelled her foul beast to lower its spiny neck. She gripped the saddle and rose up into it. Then she bid the creature to beat its dry wings, creating a dust storm about the steps and over Silaa’s remains. Finally, she spurred her new mount, the pair of them rising into the air as she did.

name: Name
body:
"I will have your head for this, Caine,"  she hissed, taking to the sky.
***

name: Name
body:
"Is that so?" Caine ran the length of the barge, parallel to the high dock where it was moored, and was suddenly confronted by a thrall laborer. The creature had leapt out of nowhere on a narrow stairwell that led down to the water. Caine blasted the creature square in the chest, his round imbued with Thunder for good measure. The thrall was sent tumbling back down the stairs and into the water with an oily splash. No sooner had the corpse hit the water than a tentacle reached up to wrap around it, pulling it under.
"I’d make a note of that, kid." Caine raised his eyes at the spectacle but did not slow down.
Cynthia agreed with a shudder as the chase continued. The thirty yard-long riverboat Caine led them down was laden with barrels marked for necrotite, and a crew of dock workers meant to unload it arrived just as they did. Their dead bodies were added to a growing tally wherever the Hellslingers went. Bane knights, too, were scattered in their wake but not nearly enough of them. The enemy’s reinforcements came, tireless in driving the Hellslingers to the barge.

name: Name
body:
Yet the drawbridge was before them at last; the extraction point was just an eight-story climb on the other side of it. As Caine now saw, it was more than the way out—it was a bottleneck for the pursuit. As he drew closer to the bridge, he spotted an iron lattice construction spanning twenty yards over the main canal into the quays, a single bascule with a raised counterweight on the near side. Notably, it was lowered and, to all appearances, safe to cross.
Caine paused before leaping overboard, spotting the way forward. The bridge seemed to operate with a control station atop a girder tower of the bridge meant to engage the counterweight to raise it. The operator would climb a ladder to a station twenty yards high that housed a single lever device on a spoked wheel spooled with thick wire. That was where he needed to be.
"What’s the play, boss?" At his side, Ryan kept an eye at the other end of the barge as more bane knights jumped down onto the deck.
"Keep moving. I’ll raise the bridge after yer across it." Caine looked back at the banes in pursuit with still more reinforcements streaming in behind them. "That should slow these jokers down."

name: Name
body:
"Take me with you," Bailoch said, struggling to reach Caine’s side.
"You sure?" Caine cocked his head. "The tower’s a double jump."
"Just go," Bailoch growled.
Caine shrugged, moving the three of them through the void twice in succession to land on the platform’s catwalk.
"Fek me." The old sniper coughed spittle over the rail, his scarred face bulging at a bad jump. Yet they were upon the grate of the counterweight tower, standing before the release controls.
"Look out!" Cynthia piped up, pointing at something over Caine’s shoulder. He turned, Spellstorm raised, to meet an incoming flock of carrion thralls. Bailoch was ready for the infernal vermin, his rifle raised and firing. Caine fired right behind him, sending a trio into the water in short order.
Bailoch struggled with one of the carrion thralls; it forced him to swing his unloaded rifle like a club, batting it away as it clawed for his face. He struck the thing square in the head, and it fell from the platform, squawking. Then Bailoch fell flat with a soft groan.

name: Name
body:
Caine blasted another pair of the hideous creatures then turned to find his sniper still down. "What’s the matter?"
"I’m fine," Kell snapped, working the action of his rifle to finish reloading it before attempting to stand again.
"No, you’re not." Caine now saw the old sniper’s duster had come open as he sat on the grate. Moreover, he saw the beads of clammy sweat and the strain on his face. And then there was the blood-soaked shirt under his jacket.
"Worry about her." Bailoch fired at an approaching bane knight as it landed on the deck of the barge below. "I’ll raise it up."
"The necrotech, was it?" Caine frowned. "Why didn’t yeh say something sooner? Anastasia could have patched yeh up."
"The bleeding is internal." Bailoch looked up from his scope, shrugged, then reloaded. "Nothing your lady friend could help me with. It was slow at first. I thought I would last longer. I was wrong."
"Kell, we can still get you clear."
"You can’t." Kell realigned his scope and fired again. "But I can keep the door shut behind you. When they start sending folks round yonder dock to get this bridge back down, I’ll keep ’em busy awhile. More’s the point, I got a nasty little surprise waiting for the first one that gets the jump on me, I’ll tell you that right now."

name: Name
body:
"Kell." Caine grimaced as the sniper reloaded again. He wasn’t kidding. "Yeh sure?"
"Dead sure." Bailoch looked at Caine with a wry smile. "I had it coming a long time."
"Thank you," Cynthia said to the sniper. Her eyes welled.
"Don’t waste those doe-eyes on me, girlie. I would have left you for dead." Bailoch killed again then hunched with a start, openly sensitive to the recoil. "It was just the smart money, understand? Your father is a maniac."
"Now you know." Caine smirked before turning serious. "I won’t forget this."
"Mind you keep your end of the bargain then." Bailoch took a breath then reloaded.
"I will."
"I got something for you too, girlie." Bailoch resighted, gritting his teeth against the pain. "I want you go with your pa when he does me that little favor. When it’s over, introduce yourself to my mama. Tell her what we did here."
Cynthia and Caine traded uncertain glances, then she looked back at Bailoch. "If you want me to, Mr. Bailoch."
"It ain’t for me." Bailoch squinted into his scope and fired, sending a bane knight into the turgid waters. Seconds later, a frenzy of the water enveloped it, dragged it down. "I just reckon she’d want to know."

name: Name
body:
"It’ll be done." Caine reloaded his own weapon then shifted Cynthia from one arm to the other, ready to leap back down.
"Get a move on, then." Bailoch aimed and fired. His shot sent another bane knight to the deck of the barge where it moved no more.
Caine tipped his Spellstorm at the dying sniper and pulled Cynthia into his leap.
On the other side, they were reunited with the Hellslingers and forced to jog midway across the bridge just to keep up. With the way ahead clear, they pressed their luck and crossed the bridge at double time. Left behind at the control station, Kell raised the bridge up after them with a fast-shifting clank of gears. For the moment at least, Deneghra’s pursuit was cut off.  Then Kell bid them go with a wave as he scanned for his next target.
"Make it count folks." Caine turned from the sight, fully convinced Bailoch would keep shooting until his dying breath. "Let’s go."
Beyond the bridge, he led the Hellslingers onward, pushing toward a crumbling entrance to the abandoned factory. As they closed in, Caine felt a sudden welling of ice in his veins. The chill running down his spine and the intuition it granted nearly whipped his face forward, where Ryan was taking point. She reached the shadowy threshold with guns leading the way only to tumble with a cry two steps inside as shots rang out.

name: Name
body:
Over her, two figures swarmed Ryan from out of the shadows with a sudden flare of spectral green. Caine could see ghostly, withered figures fighting to be the first to claim her. As they struggled, they surged with green fire that spread across Ryan. She began to scream.
"Wraiths!" Watts trained his rifle next to a horrified Anastasia.
"Get off m—" Ryan dropped her weapons, going limp. By degrees, her soul was pulled from her chest by the scrabbling phantoms’ clawing hands, a sudden tug of war erupting between them.
Before Caine could react, two more shots echoed from inside the building. An unseen shooter. As one, the wraiths fell away from Ryan, unraveling into shadow as they did. Ryan’s soul slipped back within her, and she sat up at once, coughing. As the phantoms unraveled, Caine noted a smoking bullet hole between the eyes of each.
Same as he would have done.
Again, a chill ran down his spine.
Then he saw why.
"Darcy, get back," Caine warned as something stepped from the shadows. Another luminous phantom began to materialize—but this one had his face.

name: Name
body:
"Oh, hell no." Ryan backpedaled across the ground, unable to reach her weapons as the Hellslinger wraith advanced, its pistol in hand.
The dreaded creature that was a shadow of Caine followed her to the very edge of the threshold, yet it stopped there in silence and seemingly in peace.
"Don’t shoot," Cynthia warned, placing a hand on Caine’s free arm. "He doesn’t want to fight."
"How in blazes do yeh know that?" Caine held his Spellstorm ready, shrugging Cynthia’s hand away.
"I just do."
To Caine’s surprise, his supposedly slain doppelganger did not attack. Instead, it holstered its spectral Spellstorm and stared at Cynthia.
"Didn’t I kill yeh?" Caine squinted at the thing that was him, then at Cynthia. "I killed it, didn’t I?"
The wraith laughed then, an ugly, grating rasp.
"It’s complicated," Cynthia answered. "He’s no friend of Deneghra. That much I know."
"Really?" Caine squinted at his double. The wraith ignored him, extending a hand toward Cynthia. Caine pulled her back.
"Yeh can’t have her," he growled.

name: Name
body: "No, I think he’s looking for this." Cynthia drew a spectral Spellstorm from the folds of her shirt, holding it out before her. "I, uh, borrowed it." The wraith responded at the sight of the weapon with a fervent rasp. "I don’t believe this." Caine looked back and forth between them. "He’s you, and he isn’t." Cynthia smiled meekly at her father. "But…he did help me." She tossed the weapon in a gentle lob. The creature’s fey bond with its weapon was such that as it reached out, the weapon was drawn to its grip like a magnet. And still it did not attack. Rather, it looked over the Hellslingers a moment before it turned for the shadows. "Let’s go," Cynthia urged. They ran on through the doorway; they did not see any other wraiths. Once they returned to the shadows, its creaking floors, and the dust of the factory interior, they made for the southern stairwell and dashed breathlessly for the roof. As the Hellslingers ascended to the final floor, an exposed outer wall of the crumbling structure revealed the night sky beyond and a view of Kell Bailoch’s last stand. Cynthia saw it first, pointing at the moment.

name: Name
body:
Just as Bailoch had predicted, runners were being sent across a narrow dock to take out his position and lower the bridge. He wasn’t allowing them. Bodies were piling up on the narrow path of loose planks. As Caine looked on, Bailoch scored a double headshot as a pair of thralls aligned on the dock. He tried not to get caught staring but soon blinked to find he was not alone. The Hellslingers, too were at a halt, watching the tragedy unfolding.
"No!" Cynthia saw them first, pointing with a scream.
A flock of carrion thralls surged over Kell, circling to strike. The old sniper reloaded, shooting the length of the dock again. Another kill. Then…
"Look away." Caine shielded Cynthia from the murder that descended Kell. Shrieking and casting feathers, they fell on the sniper’s nest and began to devour their prey.
"Wait for it." Watts pointed at a human hand rising from the tangle of thralls.
Caine could see the hand as well—a hand gripping a grenade. Then there was a blast of white light and shrapnel. All at once, the flock was gone. With it, Kell Bailoch. As the smoke cleared, the ruined station revealed a ruined man, the sniper’s remains scattered and smoking.

name: Name
body: "He was a good man," Ryan said. "Took the bastards with him and left them nothing to work with." "Come on." Caine kicked open the rooftop door. Bursting out into the night air, he studied the sky. "Why are we here?" Cynthia asked, confused. "Isn’t this a dead end?" "Not for us." Caine looked to the southern sky, eager for a sign of the Cloudpiercer. There was little cloud cover but for the higher reaches, yet there was no sign of the airship. He felt his skin growing colder. Where was Falk? "So yeh mean to fly me out, is that it?" Cynthia asked. "Is one of yeh gonna call down a big goony bird like Deneghra or maybe yeh got a flying ship?" "Oh, somebody told yeh then?" Caine faked a smile, turning round and round to look for a skyship he could not find. "Who told her?" "Nobody told her." Anastasia looked past Caine, searching the sky as well. Then she pointed at a faint shadow in a high cloudbank. "Is that?" "Maybe. It better be." Caine holstered his pistol to pull a flare from his jacket pocket. He twisted the cap off, setting it to spark and burn. Then he threw the flare to the center of the roof and looked up against. Amidst the glare of his marker’s flame, a billowing curl of matching smoke bellowed out over the night breeze. "I reckon we’re about to find out."

name: Name
body:
"Seriously, what are we doing on the top of a roof then." Cynthia sounded panicked.
"Seriously? We ain’t waiting on a goony bird, kid." Caine’s fact twitched. "But we might just have a flying ship."
***

name: Name
body: "Red flare. Red flare!" At the prow of the deck, the junior engineer Michaels looked down with his spyglass. The sandy-haired youth had come up from the engine room to take a station with Falk in the hope that two searchers were better than one. Behind them, the chief manned the helm while their last man, Richards, worked the engine room to keep the skydrive stoked, rationing their fuel as best he could. He had given a final warning about their reserves only moments before. And then, miraculously, the signal had come. "Where?" Falk came from the Cloudpiercer’s aft along the gunwales to join Michaels, his spyglass redirected to where the junior engineer indicated. Sure enough, a red flare. As he looked closer, he could confirm Caine and crew were gathered around the plume of colored smoke. "He’s got Cynthia all right," Michaels studied the Hellslingers, counting. "But I don’t see Bailoch." "Take us in, Chief." Falk shouted back to the helm. Yet fate seemed to have some surprises for them still as he looked overboard. Something was rising up on the Cloudpiercer’s portside’ Falk was startled to see a pair of flyers on a collision course. He took them for bonejacks at a glance, then saw the beaks of Shrikes on further magnification. He put his spyglass away and drew his scattergun and aimed from a wide-legged stance. "Bandits at four o’clock!"

name: Name
body: "Taking evasive action," the chief shouted back at helm, turning the wheel to widen the gap with their pursuers. Yet the Cloudpiercer was already committed, diving down in a tightening corkscrew to reach the Hellslingers. Now that the ship was visible to everyone below, alarms began to sound across the city. Spot-lamps were being lit; some were already sweeping the night sky after them. Falk paid it no mind. Instead, he waited for his targets to close in. As they came on, shrieking, he whispered his invocation and then pulled the trigger. His shot burst from both barrels, crackling with spectral fire. The spectacular hail shattered full force into the nearest bonejack, throwing it into a mid-air tumble that struck its partner with disastrous consequences. The second bonejack was also struck by Falk’s invocation, suffering a broken wing upon impact with its partner. It lashed out at the collision, hissing in retaliation, breaking the other’s wing with a vicious stab of its beak. Both now tumbled away to oblivion.

name: Name
body:
"What a shot!" Michaels said from the rail, raising his wrench in a cheer.
"I can do this all day." Falk holstered his scattergun and struck an overtly heroic pose, grinning as he did.
Michaels did not return the smile for long. His eyes bulged as he took in something just past Falk’s shoulder.
"Dragon," Michaels said quietly, his look dazed. Then panic took hold and he repeated, shouting, "DRAGON!"
Falk’s smile fell away as he turned to see a massive creature streaking  after them.
It was no dragon Falk saw without relief; it was a detail that would not spare them.  As he squinted to identify the winged form headed inbound, he took in a revenant monster of indescribable origins. It was serpentine in shape with a long neck that ran back to a spiny tail. It was over a dozen yards long, kept aloft by great bat-like wings framed by bony spurs, all of it wrapped in rotted canvas. It was foul, enormous, and shrouded in necrotite smoke from two iron smokestacks emerging on its shoulders.
Worst of all, the creature bore a saddle—and upon it sat Deneghra in all her deathly splendor. As she raced up toward them, an entire swarm of bonejacks trailed after her. Falk sighed.

name: Name
body:
"I just had to run my mouth, didn’t I?" He reloaded his scattergun.
***

name: Name
body: "What manner of craft is this?" Deneghra swooped around the ship, visibly perplexed by the Cloudpiercer. The Cryxian warcaster studied it intently as she flew past, drawing close enough to see Falk aiming at her only an instant before he fired. As his scattergun exploded at her with an invocation of fire, she threw her revenant beast into a roll and fell away, trading a gout of fire of her own, one vomited from her beast’s great maw. The green-hued blight fire ran along the ship’s light hull, leaving an ugly scorch down its length. As she weaved about for another look, she compelled her Scavengers to forcibly land the ship. *** A half-dozen of the chittering bonejacks fluttered past Falk, though he batted one in passing for good measure. As the Cloudpiercer descended, the Scavengers swarmed it, trying to devour it, chewing at panels and bulkheads alike. "Come on," Falk shouted to Michaels, reloading; he struggled to keep Deneghra in sight even as her minions’ boarding action raged. "Help me get them off."

name: Name
body:
"There." Michaels smashed a bonejack’s wing at the ship’s starboard side with his wrench then kicked it in the face until it fell away. "They’re going for the voltaic coils!"
"Fek." Falk popped another bonejack at point-blank range, sending it into a headless tumble.
Deneghra was already coming in for another pass. He was going to need something a little extra to take her on, and he needed it fast. If he could drive her off, the bonejacks she commanded would surely break off as well. The chief held the wheel as the descent continued; the factory rooftop loomed larger by the moment.
"We got something that burns?" Falk watched as Deneghra rose up, spiraling over them.
"Oil can. On the rack in the engine room." Michaels breathlessly bashed another bonejack attacker as it chewed a coil by his feet. It was a desperate fight—the creature sent up sparks, gnawing on the coil to short out.
"That’ll do." Falk locked eyes with Deneghra as she readied for another attack. He gripped the rail and launched himself for the engine room hatch, ducking down the stairwell below. A moment later, he reappeared on the deck with a red, briefcase-sized tin can tucked under one arm. Just as he returned, Deneghra was upon them.

name: Name
body: "Now you burn," Deneghra snarled as she drove her mount to the attack, its rotten wings flapping wide and its faceless maw priming to heave green fire at the enemy below. "You first." Falk grimaced as he punted the sloshing can straight for the creature’s looming maw. As it sailed toward the monstrosity, he raised his scattergun, firing after it with a shouted invocation of fire one more time. He watched with mounting elation as his shower of white-hot pellets struck the can. The can erupted in fire mere seconds before Deneghra’s revenant mount could launch its own attack with blight-fire. Showered by the burning oil, Deneghra shrieked—her ride was suddenly ablaze, from its eyeless face to its chest and wings. "You bastard!" she raged, struggling to keep her burning mount aloft. As the fire spread through the rotted tatters of its canvas-wrapped wings, she was forced to concede the sky, winding her mount downward in a perilous corkscrew. "That was an insane shot." Michaels ran over to Falk at the starboard rail, breathless as the bonejacks fell away with their mistress. For the moment, at least, they had saved the Cloudpiercer.

name: Name
body:
Falk flinched to find their problems had only been deferred. Deneghra and her tumbling beast were plummeting for the factory rooftop, zeroing in on the flare and the Hellslingers. Any satisfaction from his trick shot was gone as he realized he’d simply passed the buck to Caine.
Falk shrugged at Michaels. "Maybe I can’t do this all day."
***

name: Name
body:
"Flying ships are real?" Cynthia was amazed. She squinted up at the ship-like speck in the night sky above, its skydrive exhausts flaring white as it descended for them. Anastasia carefully set the girl’s broken left leg with a makeshift splint, tying rags into tight knots at her ankle.
"What did I tell yeh?" Caine looked up at her. "Think I’d pull yer broken leg?"
"But yeh have a flying ship."
"Well, technically, we stole it. We’ll sort that part out later."
"If there is a later," Anastasia added in Llaelese, releasing her patient back to her father on a tentative step. "Try not to put too much weight on it, dear."
"So not only are flying ships real," Cynthia limped a step before she was scooped back into Caine’s shoulder with an awestruck smile, "yeh stole one, just for me?"
"I did." Caine pointed to Ace by the stairwell. "And that big hunk of scrap over there besides."
"Yer bad." Cynthia smiled.
"Movement downstairs." Ryan covered the stairwell with Ace; they both now turned to Caine. "Bane knights and wall-to-wall thralls, folks."

name: Name
body: "Was only a matter of time." Caine drew a Spellstorm. "Come on, Falk. Hurry the hell up." "Boss?" Watts was focused up, tracking something across the sky with his rifle’s scope. "He’s not alone up there." At Watts’ gesture, Caine squinted and recognized the green blaze of soul-fire exhaust and a wyrm’s serpentine twisting across the sky. The creature was on an intercept course with the Cloudpiercer escorted by a flock of winged bonejacks. He knew the shape well enough and had long ago come to despise it. He had battled the thing before—with Deneghra at its reins. Counting the necrotite soul-fire exhaust plumes encircling her, he determined she had brought a dozen bonejacks with her at least. "Overkill much, lady?" he sighed. As the Cloudpiercer came for them in an erratic corkscrew, he could see flashes of mage fire from its deck. "Aye, Falk!" Watts shouted, stealing glances between the sky with his scope and the stairwell with his own eyes. "Give ’em hell, buddy." As Deneghra closed the gap, Falk surprised them all with an incendiary shot like nothing they’d ever seen, instantly setting most of the revenant creature ablaze in a spectacular fireball.

name: Name
body:
"Did he invoke that?" Ryan gasped. "No way. Did he just invoke that?"
Caine dismissed the commentary, watching in silence as Deneghra was forced into damage control with her mount. As its wings burned, it was clear that she was no longer flying—she was falling. Yet as he calculated her descent, he realized she was falling straight at them. In moments, it became unavoidable. Only a few dozen yards overhead, she was plummeting down right on top of them, bonejacks streaking in after her.
"Get close," Caine shouted, eyes on the stairwell with an impending crowd. There was only one place to go, and it wasn’t here. It was the place between places.
Deneghra’s flaming bulk was directly over them now, the heat of its ruined wings beating flames down upon them. Caine opened a portal, pulling the Hellslingers through the void.
Then Deneghra struck—and they were gone. Her impact crushed the rooftop, shattering it into a collapsed bowl between floors. As she came down, her escort of Scavenger and Shrike bonejacks landed in a haphazard circle around her. They hissed steam intended for prey through their fangs and beaks alike, only for it to vanish.

name: Name
body:
On the other side of the leap, Caine brought the Hellslingers through unscathed, though unsettled. He reappeared directly in front of the sprawling revenant, his Spellstorm focusing his attention. His aim easily found Deneghra as she fought to control her beast. The shot that followed was unerring, a spectral streak aimed directly at her head. In her distraction, he did not miss.
The warwitch’s power field burst, and she screamed with inhuman rage. Arcane power arced away from her, coursing through her mount and into the crumbling roof. Adding insult to injury, the shot sent her tumbling from her saddle, backpedaling into the rubble.
"Deneghra." Caine holstered his Spellstorm as she struggled up from behind cover. "Let me make this clear. My little girl here ain’t joining yer silly circus of mince-meat freaks."
"You forget your place." Deneghra restored her power field as she stepped clear of the rubble. She put one hand on her smoldering beast, bringing it under control, and raised her staff to contend with Caine. By degrees, she recovered, her stricken beast rising up on the skeletal bladed spars of its ruined wings, readying to belch blight fire at her command.

name: Name
body: "Do I?" Caine held his ground, Cynthia in his arm. Around the Hellslingers, Caine saw Deneghra’s bonejacks tightening the loop, creeping closer, held from an outright charge by her will alone. As he glanced over at the stairwell exit, he could see bane knights arriving on the scene to seal them off. They, too, were oddly restrained, snarling and hissing as they waited for the word to be given. Deneghra smiled as she recovered, satisfied in her assessment of the confrontation. "Look around you. This chase is over. Now give me the girl." "It’s not going to happen." Caine squinted past Deneghra for the inbound Cloudpiercer. "I reckon it’s past time yeh saw the writing on the wall." The skyship descended, getting closer with each moment. As it came into a better view, Caine noticed a fire had broken out amongst the starboard coils. An engineer was beating at the flames, and it canted ten degrees to port, but the helm was keeping her steady. He locked eyes with Deneghra. Caine needed a moment. He needed a moment for Falk to close the gap. He needed a moment to build focus, as much as he could. He needed a moment to catch his breath, but more than all that, he needed a moment to clear the air with the one who had taken his child from him.

name: Name
body:
"What are you talking about?" Deneghra demanded, pausing in her advance.
"Yeh already lost this fight, witch. I’m just the one here to tip yeh over." Caine’s humor was gone; his features turned cruel. "My little girl by her lonesome took everything yeh had and threw it all back in yer face. Made a fool of yeh in front of Toruk himself with a merry little chase. Didn’t she? Seems to me that’s something yer pitiful mug couldn’t manage when Satyxis brought yeh here all those years ago. Do I have that about right?"
Caine’s jabs landed. He saw a tremor pass over Deneghra’s dead features, curling her lip by reflex.
"None of that will matter when I offer him your head and take Cynthia for my apprentice," she growled, glowing as her power field was restored.
"Yeh want her so bad?" His free hand hovered over his holstered Spellstorm. He winked at Cynthia. "Then draw."
He waited, his hand steady as focus surged through his veins. His words had unleashed the wrath he’d carried since the day of Cynthia’s abduction. For her part, Cynthia gave a knowing smile and reached for his other pistol.

name: Name
body: Deneghra could not resist the taunt. Her spear began crackling with arcane light, a sickly green at its tip. As she aimed the slender weapon to unload a scourge upon them, Caine drew his Spellstorm with a practiced easy motion that seemed a blur. He leapt skyward, through a portal aimed five yards overhead. Underneath them, Deneghra’s scourge bolt found the place they had just been, scorching an empty spot. Caine invoked a Maelstrom and opened fire. The whole world was spinning, faster and faster with each rotation. His first shot drove a bonejack from the rooftop ledge, the creature’s jaw exploding like plaster dust. Then another was blasted in its midriff, collapsing. Another fell and then another. As he and Cynthia continued to spin in circles, he glanced to the approach of the Cloudpiercer and knew the moment was nearly upon them. Another fell. Just a few seconds more… Cynthia aimed his other Spellstorm herself. Caine let his focus channel through her, guiding her hand as if it were his own. Then she fired, sending a bonejack over the rooftop ledge as soul fire escaped from the grievous gut wound she had dealt it.

name: Name
body: They blasted shot after shot until at last their spinning brought Deneghra into their crosshairs.  Caine set Cynthia on her, raising his own Spellstorm to target her flying beast just as it reared up to rain down fire. He invoked thunder and let fly. The shot burst from his weapon with an arcane blaze as loud as its namesake.

name: Name
body:
Cynthia opened fire at Deneghra as the warwitch’s staff surged with the green spellfire of another scourge—a split second too late. Cynthia’s Spellstorm erupted as her father’s did, imbued beyond the muzzle with all the power he could spare.
Both shots struck true. Caine’s shot exploded the chin of the beast’s open maw, snapping its neck brutally back, tilted up and away.
Cynthia’s shot caught Deneghra square in the chest, at once erupting with a roiling blast that burst her power field again. She stumbled back on loose footing to the very ledge, her grip on her staff loosening.
"Look," Cynthia said, watching the horror spread across Deneghra’s features as the witch fell back into empty air.
"Well played." Caine watched Deneghra fall.
Then, the maelstrom was over.
Deneghra disappeared over the side of the roof with a scream. All but a pair of the bonejacks were gone; their escape route was cleared of enemies. Even as it rose up over them, Deneghra’s mount had been diverted by Caine’s whiplash, its bale fire spewing directly up like a geyser. As it reached its peak, the acrid fire fell back to earth, coating the creature with fire a second time. It roared in dismay, burning and disoriented.

name: Name
body: The Hellslingers meant to finish the creature. Ace fired at it, driving it back. Watts added another shot aimed for a chink in its chest furnace that sent it recoiling again. Ryan fired both pistols at the thing’s widened maw, breaking teeth that further decimated it. Anastasia lobbed the last of her charges—it exploded nearly on contact, blowing open a horrific wound in the creature’s thick coiled tail. The withering attack from all of them sent the creature thrashing in a retreat, blinded, burning, until at last it tumbled after its lost master over the side. Caine saw the Cloudpiercer streaking for them now, its fires still burning but seemingly under control. As it drew closer, he saw the moment was upon them. Despite the carnage, they were not safe—bane knights were now flooding through the stairwell to stop them, their numbers seemingly unlimited. "We are leaving," Caine shouted, readying a portal as the Cloudpiercer leveled in near them, hovering alongside the rooftop ledge to their left. They had only seconds to get clear. "Stay close!"

name: Name
body: He took a deep breath and ran for the ledge. The Hellslingers followed as he opened the void to take them across the gap. An instant too late, he saw the tail emerge from below the ledge, its bladed tip quickly curling itself around Cynthia’s foot. Anastasia saw it at the same time, wide-eyed horror. Then Cynthia was gone, snatched away screaming as she disappeared. They leapt without her. The Hellslingers reappeared on the deck of the passing Cloudpiercer. "No!" Caine shouted scrambling for the railing. Below, he could see Deneghra, triumphant, remounted on her revenant beast as the creature gripped the side of the factory with the bladed claws of its ruined wings. In the coil of its tapering tail, Cynthia screamed. Anastasia grabbed Caine’s arm. "Can’t you just…take her back?" "If they’re tangled up, I’m as likely to take them both." He shook off her grip and then shouted to the helm of the Cloudpiercer. "Bring her in!" "I’ll cut her loose." Anastasia drew her blades. "Just you be ready to pull us back."

name: Name
body:
Caine nodded as she prepared a running leap for the ascending beast, her weapons ready. "Be careful."
She jumped.
She landed by plunging both knives into the beast’s flank just behind Deneghra’s saddle. Her momentum tore ribbons down the tail. She grappled around to the creature’s spine before Deneghra could draw a bead on her.
Caine marveled at Anastasia’s attack; the lady had both skills and stones. He watched her climb down the jutting spines as easily as a ladder and proceed to hack the tapered end coiled about Cynthia. With a few slashes of her blade, the tail grew limp and began to gush ichor. Cynthia wriggled out and reached for Anastasia’s hand.
"Get us out of here!" Anastasia looked to Caine from across the gap, clinging to Cynthia and life as the wraith engine thrashed to shake them both loose.
"You will die now." Deneghra was turning in her saddle, her spear aimed at Anastasia. She loosed a scourge across Anastasia’s cheek, its corrupting touch tracing a deadly line that withered her cloak. Anastasia was forced to scramble away to avoid being hit and dislodged. Her grip on Cynthia broke—both of them were left dangling, Anastasia by only one hand gripping the creature’s spine.

name: Name
body: Caine drew focus. "Hang on." He vanished from the deck of the Cloudpiercer, reappearing mid-air over Deneghra’s thrashing mount. Time froze long enough for Caine to take it all in: Deneghra, Cynthia, and Anastasia all stared at him, each desperate in her own way. He reached wide with his gift, feeling Cynthia and Anastasia as it enveloped them. He formed a portal for the three of them and centered it over the deck of the Cloudpiercer. Against the strain and cognizant of his flagging reserves, he opened the void… Deneghra struck. Caine was at once grappled by the bleeding stump of the beast’s tail, his focus lost and his portal gone. He choked as it encircled his throat. Then he was airborne—Deneghra commanded her beast to dangle him before her so she could watch him suffocate. Anastasia and Cynthia clung helplessly to the creature’s backside, a fatal fall waiting below them. "Am I weak now?" Deneghra shrieked, bringing Caine up to hang upside down before her. She aimed her spear at him, ready to loose its magic upon him. "Am I?"

name: Name
body: He could barely heard her taunt, let alone return it. He was blacking out. Focus lost, he saw with increasing tunnel vision the Cloudpiercer circling nearby. The Hellslingers were blasting supporting fire at the beast to free him. Ace was there, looking down at him but growing blurry in his dimming sight. Then Ace was leaping. He struggled to make sense of what he was seeing: His warjack was suddenly midair, falling straight for him, axe raised high to strike. "No!" Deneghra saw Ace too late as he plummeted directly at her. The warjack’s landing not only unseated Deneghra from her mount, but Ace brought his axe down hard, lodging it deep in the serpent’s shoulder. The wound broke the wing; it went limp. With Ace’s added weight now to bear, the creature was hopelessly torn from the wall and sent tumbling. Caine felt the tail uncoil as they fell and struggled to get himself clear, horribly aware that all of them were hurtling toward their deaths. The battle between the tangled wraith engine and the warjack continued even as they all fell. With the last of its strength, the wyrm’s good wing raked Ace off, sending him into a cartwheeling freefall of his own.

name: Name
body: Groggy and plummeting upside down, Caine struggled for focus. Anastasia and Cynthia were close enough, but Ace was fading, lost to his magical sight. Above him, Cloudpiercer approached, Falk at the prow. Caine silently cursed the ground as it rushed up to meet him, but in his anger, he found the last of his strength. Finally, he opened the void and pulled them through to the other side. On the deck of the Cloudpiercer, he reappeared, landing hard and knocking the wind out of himself. He rolled over, wheezing, to find Cynthia and Anastasia both gasping for breath. Ace was not with them. Still winded, Caine dragged himself to the rail and looked overboard. On the ground far below, he could just make out his warjack—Ace had smashed to pieces on impact from the long fall, lying next to the bulk of the ruined creature. Though Deneghra was nowhere to be seen, thralls swarmed the area, picking over his lost warjack. "I’m sorry, chum." Caine slumped, overcome and exhausted at last. "Yeh deserved better."

name: Name
body:
"You all right, boss?" Falk came to his side, taking a knee.
Caine nodded feebly, struggling to speak. The ground below him seemed to swirl.
Anastasia joined them, helping to get him propped up. She glanced at Falk. "Get us out of here, Bastion."
Then Caine blacked out.

name: Name
body:
"Keep looking. Move!" Vilkul commanded her hounds. She stepped over the body of the Cygnaran duty clerk as the search for the Orgoth artifact continued.
Past the duty clerk’s desk, the long tent had been divided into three rows of well-stocked shelves and an inventory on palettes, all dimly lit by strings of electric lamps. Crates, barrels, and bushels of all sorts lined the way, marked by numbered signposts for placement.
Vilkul was irked. The artifact had been hidden from her, without a doubt. Its presence at the depot was undeniable yet oddly muffled. A lead-lined case perhaps? Why would Rosko have taken such a precaution? Vilkul’s arcane senses reached out to no avail. Wherever it was, they would have to find it the hard way.
She brooded over calculations as she probed ahead. It was, of course, only a matter of time until someone discovered that all of the personnel at the supply depot and the airfield adjacent to it were dead. It followed, then, that it was only a matter of time until the alarm would be raised, and SKS-6 would need to disappear. As she worked her way down the long aisle, pulling back tarps and prying open crates, it occurred to her she did much care for playing games with Captain Rosko.

name: Name
body:
Razor had been left back at the front gate checkpoint as a precaution. He waited, hidden within the checkpoint tent, to watch for unwanted visitors.
