While Skrobola and Fedyniak examined the aisles adjacent her own, Teterya and Lazarenko proceeded outside to investigate the dozen smaller neighboring tents that made up the depot’s gridded layout of a few acres square.
"I have something." Fedyniak was the first to call out from across the aisle after what seemed a minor eternity to Vilkul. As she rushed over, she found Skrobala alongside him with a prybar, working loose the planks off a large crate to reveal a reinforced iron crate hidden inside. Its markings indicated the highest security, and she felt a pulse of arcane dread to be this close to it.
"Yes, that’s it." Vilkul turned toward the sudden arrival of Lazarenko.
Her Jackal was flushed of face as he pointed his thumb back the way he had come. "Movement outside the picket. Could be a patrol. Whoever they are, they have a warjack."
Vilkul regarded the metal crate while Skrobola struggled with the heavy lock upon it. A frown knit her face. "Get ready."

name: Name
body:
"Awful quiet," Caine observed as he approached the supply depot on a dirt road that divided the woods south of Merrin. With his Hellslingers beside him, he paused to regard the silence at the front gate. He took a knee and produced a spyglass from his jacket as Watts and Ryan joined him.
"What ya see, boss?" Watts cocked his rifle.
"Nothing and nobody," Caine whispered, lingering his lens over the front gate. "That ain’t right."
Merrin was a ghost town as many fled. Those who were willing to stay were under curfew at this time of night. The supply depot was not under Merrin’s control, however. It was of continuous use to allies and was constantly guarded—no one manned the gate, and nothing moved within the perimeter. Nevertheless, Caine’s arcane senses were alerted with a steady, dull throb that made him want to retch. There was no question: The artifact was here.
"You think SKS-6 got here first?" Ryan suggested.
"Maybe. If they are, they haven’t taken the artifact. Can’t yeh feel it?"
"Yeah." Ryan concentrated, flexing her own Gift with a hand to her temple. "It’s muddled, but—"

name: Name
body:
"What’s the play, Major?" Falk stood ready behind Caine, gripping his magelock.
"I’m going to go scout the depot by my lonesome." Caine stood up, cracked his neck, and put his spyglass in his jacket pocket. "See who I can flush out."
To Deuce, Caine gave a side-eyed glance and a singular thought. His warjack nodded, dutifully keeping silent, then turned to go.
"Where’s he off to?" Glover looked after the ’jack as he moved for the tree line to the south, closest to the depot’s picket fence.
"He’s going to take cover until I need him."
"Where do you need Swansong?" Watts raised his scoped rifle, running a loving hand down its polished stock.
"I need yeh up there. Take Ryan. Cover me but hold yer fire unless there’s nothing else for it."
"Of course." Watts was already moving as Ryan turned to follow.
"What about us?" Glover looked to Falk and back to Caine, pressing his tricorn into place on his head.
"Same as Deuce, I reckon," Caine said. "Take east and west of the perimeter and lay low for my signal. If it gets hairy in there, I’ll jump back out the way I came."

name: Name
body:
"You got it." Falk was moving for the gate then dropped down to lay prone using the ditch for cover.  Glover stalked past him, looking for cover on the east side of the depot.
Satisfied at last, Caine holstered his Spellstorms and started for the gate. No challenge—no one came out to meet him. As he walked through the checkpoint, he started whistling a cheerful tune to draw attention. There was still no response, but there was a presence his Gift began to sense ahead. Without a doubt, he could feel another warcaster ahead.
He continued whistling as he made his way to the long quartermaster’s tent at the center of the depot. He opened its flap and pushed his way inside. There was a flurry of hurried movement in the back, hushed chatter. Shadowy figures in bulky armor were gathered alongside a crate in the leftmost aisle. All of them looked up at his arrival, but none of them moved.
"Under new management, is it?" Caine leaned over the countertop; it had been freshly wiped down. A tin cup sat to the side, with a single blood drop on it. "Missed a spot."

name: Name
body:
"Major Caine," A woman’s voice replied evenly from the group. The accent was Khadoran with a Volningrad dialect. "I have been expecting you."
Zahara Vilkul emerged with a calm expression the shadows. Caine saw she was wearing the thick red-and-black plates of Khadoran warcaster armor, distinguished by a rack of four angled posts sprouting from its back. She carried an axe at her side, but she did not bother to raise it. Despite the bulk of her kit, she moved as lithely as a lioness. The analogy seemed apt to Caine, feeling the hair on the back of his neck rise the closer she came.
"Kapitan Vilkul." Caine stepped back from the counter to take a wide-footed stance.
"It seems we are both well informed."
"I should hope so. It sure don’t come cheap."
As he spoke, a mustached man quickly entered the tent behind him and drove a menacing pistol against his back. Caine turned slowly, hands raised to find the one they called Lazarenko winking at him while chewing a toothpick, the sheer bulk of his Kommando armor and the oversized bazooka slung at his shoulder belying the utter silence in which he moved.

name: Name
body:
The trio of shadowy figures he saw gathered by the crate at the end of the aisle moved to join them, their weapons drawn and eyes narrowed. Under the lamplight, Caine could now see they wore the same bulky Khadoran Kommando armor as Lazarenko.
"SKS-6, as I live and breathe." Caine smiled. "Well, did yeh find it?"
"You appear to have me at a disadvantage." Vilkul seemed intrigued. "Please, explain."
"The disadvantage is all mine." He looked around at the weapons drawn on him.
"We know Oriax isn’t the only one looking for it," he replied. "What we don’t know is how you caught wind of it."
"There is little that happens that Section Three does know about." Vilkul allowed herself a slight smile. "Did you really believe we were just going to let Cygnar claim an object of such power for themselves?"
"So, yeh got no idea what it does either, do yeh?"
Vilkul paused, studying Caine’s expression as if she might discern some clue to the artifact’s true nature. "We will worry about that later."
"And here I thought we were allies."

name: Name
body:
"I think this conversation has come to an end, don’t—?" Vilkul began, then spotted the grenade that had rolled to her feet.
"Get down, Kapitan!" Lazarenko abandoned Caine to throw Vilkul behind the counter as the remaining Hounds dove for cover.
Caine smiled, watching them go. Then he opened the void and vanished.
The explosion’s shockwave shook the tent, tearing it asunder above them. The front half collapsed, leaving the Hounds struggling to get out from under it.
Caine reappeared outside the tent to watch. Next to him stood Anastasia di Bray, another grenade at the ready, her finger within the pin.
"Right where I said they’d be, no?" Anastasia said in Llaelese, watching the Hounds twisting beneath the canvas. "You have lost the wager."
"Payment forthcoming, darlin’," Caine said. "Now we know why they’re here."
Vilkul fought clear of the tent, fiery magic churning around her as runes formed over her hands.
"You will regret that," she growled, raising her axe.
"Show me," Caine said, his Spellstorms drawn.

name: Name
body:
"For fek’s sake, will you stop moving?" Cynthia drove her blade down over and again into the exposed back of the assault reaver at her feet, spattering them both with his blood.
Moments earlier, her rocket had blown the charging man’s leg entirely off, but in his rage or shock, he came crawling to reach her just the same, knife in hand, before she could reload.
The gruesome duel ended at last with a brutal neck strike. With the reaver’s death, the latest enemy rush collapsed. Cynthia wiped her blade and dared a look ahead to the shattered line and the bridge beyond. Many Orgoth still crossed. Her heart raced as it dawned on her that this could be a losing fight, even without Oriax and his Gharlghast. As she closed the receiver shut for her launcher, she was thankful that she had not yet run out of rockets.
The Invaders had kept the Gravediggers in the fight this long by ferrying ammunition and supplies to the bridge from the southern depot on a nearly endless loop since they had made landfall in the afternoon. Just the same, each grunt lost cost them dearly. Ten Gravediggers were all that remained of Cynthia’s platoon, with a pair of Patriots and Pokey in support. She knew no amount of ammunition would help if there were no was no one left alive to use it.

name: Name
body:
As Furious Finn passed by overhead, Cynthia glanced up and sighed with relief to see a pair of triple-chuted crates coming down, each bearing the telltale stencils of modular barricades. Such fortifications were badly needed since their hastily dug line of timber and earthworks had been smashed by the Gharlghast. The resulting gaps had allowed each Orgoth attack to crash into them time and again.
"Get those assembled, right now!" Cynthia pointed to the crates as they fell to earth ahead of her. The closest of her Gravediggers sprang up from their positions to comply. As they did, she directed her warjacks to provide covering fire.
As the shooting continued, it occurred to Cynthia that she might have overreacted to her father. In truth, he and his Hellslingers were no less her family despite the years of absence their penance to Rebald had required.
Cynthia replayed her words in her head, wondering if they would be the last her father heard. As the barricades rose up, she took position and, joined by her grunts, tracked her next target downrange. Maybe they had a shot after all…

name: Name
body:
A sudden vision of terror gripped Cynthia, breaking her concentration. The violent imagery forced her to a knee; her nearby lieutenant reacted quickly.
"What’s the matter?" Sergeant Baxter fired over the barricade alongside Cynthia as she faltered, gripped by vertigo.
"It’s my fa—" She struggled, trying to make sense of what was happening. "The Hellslingers… They’re in bad trouble."
"Oriax?" Baxter reloaded, glancing her way.
"Yes," She had seen the Orgoth warlord in her vision, front and center against her father. "But there’s someone else."
With deep breaths, she sorted through the flood of images that had nearly knocked her over. Her father was facing Oriax alone, or so it seemed. How could that happen? Where were the Hellslingers? She saw Deuce destroyed, Watts and Ryan lying dead nearby. The rest of the Hellslingers were gone. There were Khadorans, too—but not on their side.
"What is it?" Baxter asked.
"We need to go. Right away,"
"What about the refugees? We can’t leave them to this mob."

name: Name
body:
"No." Cynthia studied the bridge, looking behind her to the Ordic highway.
"What then?" Baxter demanded, finding a target for his next shot between glances at Cynthia.
Just in front of them, a fresh wave of reavers met the barricades, struggling to get over. Her Gravediggers were brutal, sticking them with bayonets and point-blank shots alike as they tried to climb over. As the last man in the wave fell dead on the other side, Baxter looked back at Cynthia.
"What are your orders?"
"Signal both Invaders to dump their remaining ammunition. I want it all on the bridge. On my mark."
"Ma’am?" Sargent Baxter raised an eyebrow as he looked downrange. "You want the enemy to have it?"
"Look there." Cynthia pointed.
Past the gore of the heaped bodies before them, near the embattled center of the bridge, the ground had become uneven—the piers beneath them had been visibly weakened by repeated blasts throughout the battle. Baxter nodded as it dawned on him.
"I’m going to put the Tague Bridge out of our misery." Cynthia patted her rocket launcher. "That should buy the refugees time to get clear."

name: Name
body:
"Yes, Ma’am." The sergeant drew flares from his vest pocket. "We need to push them back first, get them behind the drop."
"Acknowledged." Cynthia took stock of her firing line of warjacks behind the barricades.
Alongside Pokey, the newly dropped Patriots 448 and 509 were keeping the Orgoth harried with cannon fire at range and a flamethrower when they drew near. While Cynthia saw 509’s fuel gauge was down to less than half the tank, she knew it would be enough for one more push. As she took over the warjack, it stepped ahead of the barricades with a vicious gout that washed over the nearest Orgoth.
"Throw the flares." Cynthia turned to Baxter. "509 is going to clear a path for us."
***

name: Name
body:
Caine was in the thick of the firefight, down behind crates as the fiery slugs of a chain gun whizzed overhead. The supply depot had become a shooting gallery, with suffocating smoke, tents ablaze, and burning crates wherever SKS-6 moved. Ash flakes tumbled in the air under Vilkul’s magic, reminding Caine of the night sky in Skell so long ago.
Anastasia’s forewarning and the Hellslingers’ ambush had caught SKS-6 flatfooted, and they were being hemmed in by degrees. Caine knew if he could just get the drop on Vilkul, the firefight would be over quickly. But finding her in a burning maze was easier said than done. Her Gift made her squad nigh invisible to spot. Even with his gift of teleportation, leaping blind was as likely to get him killed. No doubt, Vilkul knew this too.
Caine reckoned Vilkul’s reputation as a peerless strategist was well earned as he watched her alternate between distraction and brute force in skillful combination. Wherever she was, she was using cover the same as he was, or else she was creating it with her Gift, guiding her team to maximum effect.

name: Name
body:
A straight-up fight, they could have managed. There was no time for hide and seek. Oriax was undoubtedly coming. Caine felt the tension rising with every traded shot. He needed the fight over and over quickly. Risks were quickly becoming unavoidable.
As the crate Caine was hugging splintered under Skrobola’s withering chain-gun hail, he reconsidered his options. He looked across the pitch to his Hellslingers, hugging cover of their own and leaning out for quick shots as the opportunity presented. Deuce alone stood exposed in the pitch, striding directly for the chain gunner. His cannon double-tapped, pressing the SKS-6 chain gunner to retreat behind a stack of crates.
"Just like the old days?" Sitting with her back to the crate, Anastasia, knives drawn, smiled at him..
"No time to reminisce, darlin’."
"Like I said."
"Keep their attention," Caine said, relaying the message to Watts and Ryan with hand gestures. "I’m going to try to flank ’em."
Watts nodded first, firing blind over his head then pointing in the direction he suspected hidden targets.

name: Name
body:
"Be ready," Caine signaled, reloading.
"How about a grenade?" Anastasia sheathed a blade, producing the explosive from her pouch.
"Over there." Caine indicated the chain gunner’s last known position, snapping his Spellstorms shut for emphasis. He waited until she’d thrown it over the crates, and then he vanished into the void, reappearing a few yards away behind new cover.
After the grenade detonated, he peered over his crates to discover the Hounds’ left flank. A pair of Vilkul’s Kommandos were picking themselves up off the ground in the aftermath of the blast, dazed though not badly injured, thanks to their considerable body armor. He also spotted Vilkul’s warjack Razor moving in on Anastasia.
"Fek." Caine squeezed off a pair of shots at Razer to draw his attention, knowing full well he would be seen by Vilkul through her warjack’s eyes if he kept shooting.
Then keep moving, he thought as his heart raced. He leaped again, this time risking the cover of burning crates closer to where Watts had indicated. As he peered from behind his new cover, he spotted the one they called the Jackal, easily identifiable by his hefty bazooka.

name: Name
body:
The veteran Kommando was reloading his weapon, no doubt angling to put Deuce out of action. Yet Razor still seemed to have Caine’s scent. The warjack’s stomping advance now beelined in his direction, chainsaw whirring. He took a breath and launched himself into a short sprint for the Jackal, Spellstorms leading.
"Hey, chum," Caine taunted in passing, firing twice at the Kommando’s exposed backside before sliding into new cover. Two shots, two hits.
Caine was sure he’d lost Razor and the Jackal was down, but he couldn’t confirm the kill from his new position. Instead, he saw something even better. At Caine’s nine-o’clock, there she was: Vilkul poked her head around the corner only a moment to direct her troops with a gesture, but Caine saw enough. As far as he could tell, she had not seen him.
"You are outmatched, Major," she shouted across the pitch without looking his way. "A fatal mistake."
A second later, Caine understood: Razor’s massive chainsaw sent him diving, erupting suddenly through the crates he was using as cover. The warjack followed up by crashing through the crates wholesale, destroying his cover completely.

name: Name
body:
"Ease off." Caine’s eyes bulged as the warjack kept coming, forcing him into the void.
On the other side, he appeared behind Vilkul.
"Call off your dogs," Caine growled, both barrels aimed at the back of her head. "I have you dead to rights."
"So it would seem." Vilkul grudgingly dropped her blades and raised her hands.
"Call them," Caine ordered, kicking her weapons from her feet. "Do it now."
Vilkul complied. Caine remained rooted to the spot behind her. Moments later, the Hounds appeared, their weapons dropped. Razor stepped forward slowly, appearing compliant. Yet even as it lowered its ugly weapon, Caine sensed the tension in its frame. He wasn’t entirely sure he had control of the situation.
"Hellslingers, on me," he shouted. "I have Vilkul."
The advancing warjack was suddenly moving toward Caine again, chainsaw whirring. Sensing his distraction, Vilkul made her play. She dove down, reaching for her weapon as the warjack lunged.
Two shots rang out, and Razor’s chainsaw was gone. Where it had been, a tangled mess of rods and wire remained, hissing with steam. Deuce stepped forward with two smoking barrels, steadfast in his master’s defense.

name: Name
body:
But Vilkul was not done. As she reached for her axe, Caine whirled around to shoot it away from her. She turned to face him from the ground, snarling as she found his smoking barrels now pointed at her face.
"I hear yer a big Reign player," Caine said. "I reckon that’s checkmate, lady."
As the remaining Hellslingers emerged from their positions, the leader of SKS-6 did not answer; instead, she fumed. Caine noted the Jackal had not yet surrendered himself as her Hounds had but was soon found nonetheless, groaning where Caine had left him.
"What do you want me to do with this one?" Glover stood over the Jackal, holding his magelock on the wounded Kommando.
Caine did not have the time to answer. Before he could open his mouth, a whistling sound tore the air. He reeled as sudden, overwhelming trauma from his warjack blasted into his own senses. Breathless, he turned to Deuce.
Two iron bolts, each a meter long, had pierced Deuce’s voltaic generators. Sparks and smoke erupted from his warjack’s power source as it died, frozen in place. With a flicker, the light in Deuce’s eyes went out.

name: Name
body:
From the nearby tree line adjacent to the supply depot, the powerful and resonant footfalls of a large herd echoed. Five mighty siege tarasks emerged, following a masked figure as grim as death itself on horseback. The horse leapt over the supply depot’s picket fence as ensorcelled bolts leapt from the outstretched hand of its rider. The twelve-foot-tall siege tarasks did not bother to step over the picket—they trampled and smashed their way through it to keep pace with their master.
Oriax had arrived.
"Fall back!" Caine commanded, turning from the charge to dive for cover as Oriax’s hex blast blackened the earth at his feet. Vilkul was already gone, her hounds likewise backpedaling for cover. Following his warcaster’s lead, Razor conceded the pitch as well.
The Hellslingers withdrew firing at the tarasks’ vulnerable riders. One fell from the saddle like a stone; another clutched at a gut shot, but the beasts continued to force Caine’s squad to retreat.
For the moment, the Hellslingers would have to fend for themselves. As Oriax bore straight down on Caine, he launched himself from his mount, soul flayer whirling to strike.

name: Name
body:
Still reeling from losing Deuce’s loss, Caine managed only a half-step and a roll to avoid the incoming flail. The weapon’s weighted soul cage head caught his leg, searing through his power field. His leg blazed with an agonizing pain that upended him. Oriax attacked again, driving his flail for Caine over and over. Caine scrambled to get back on his feet, raising a Spellstorm in his defense only to have it struck away by the next blow of Oriax’s flail. As he put his weight on his still tingling leg, Caine stumbled and fell again. His leg was broken.
Oriax took him by the throat, lifting him up off his feet entirely. Caine choked, felt Oriax’s free hand reaching for his chest, felt an indescribable pain there. By reflex, he used the last of his focus for a leap, back for the cover he’d been hugging so surely only moments before. As he reappeared through the void, he slumped down, forced to reload his single Spellstorm from the ground.
At a glance, he saw Watts and Ryan playing give and go to keep ahead of a siege tarask across the smoky pitch. As it lumbered through the smoldering fires after them, it smashed aside their cover with brutal swipes wherever they led. He looked away from their plight, took a deep breath, and made to stand on one leg, readying his weapon.

name: Name
body:
Violently shouting in his native tongue, Oriax’s voice was shrill, muffled behind his mask.
Caine didn’t understand the Orgoth language, but he didn’t need to. He heard the rattle of footsteps approaching, and he knew Oriax was coming for his soul.
***

name: Name
body: "The major needs us," Cynthia shouted to helm from the prow of the Cracker Barrel, the wind in her hair and a fire in her eyes. "Hurry!" The embattled Invader dove through the night sky at full throttle, engines whining and deck plates shaking with strain and battle damage alike. Furious Finn followed in close after them, equally red-lining and damaged. The cause of the damage was easy enough to discern—the gore of rhok harriers was smeared over the decks and soldiers alike. But that was all. The battle of the Tague Bridge had been won, no matter the rhoks that had been drawn to battle, no matter that the bridge had been blown, and no matter the cost in lives. Not when the fate of Cynthia’s father, his Hellslingers, and the very artifact they had been sent to retrieve all hung in the balance now. Thanks to her Gift, Cynthia felt her father’s desperation in her bones, and it spurred her on. Cynthia's bond with her father, first forged in Skell all those years ago, had continued to grow as she matured into a warcaster. Moreover, it was a two-way conduit. She knew something had gone very wrong; he was in pain, crippled even. Though he would never admit it to anyone, she could sense his fear. Yet pain and fear could be managed. Such impressions meant at the very least she wasn’t too late. In the next moment or the one that followed? She could not say.

name: Name
body:
"Come on." She pounded the rail with one hand while adjusting the straps of her harness with the other. She watched Merrin scroll beneath her seemingly in slow motion. The southern supply depot was close but felt distant still as a pang of torment suddenly flared via their connection. The pain was excruciating. Moreover, she could feel soul magic in it.
Oriax was there.
More than this, she sensed the Orgoth warlord had the upper hand. To her arcane senses, his sickly magic was a radiant beacon in the dark of night. Her father had moments to live. As the supply depot came into focus below, she was ready.
Behind her, her embattled Gravediggers stood ready at the rail in their drop harnesses, grim-faced and loaded for battle. Her once full-strength platoon had been reduced to a mere eight souls, yet all of them knew the debt they owed the Hellslingers. Despite their wounds and an exhausting day of battle, not a grunt among them would duck this fight. Despite her fears, the truth was she had never been prouder.

name: Name
body: As the Invaders closed in on the supply depot from an altitude of twenty-four hundred feet, Cynthia had waited long enough. "Gravediggers, jump!" She was over the rail and into a breathless freefall. Behind her, the Gravediggers followed suit, spaced at ten-yard intervals. Pokey spilled out after from the ramp at the back of Cracker Barrel’s hold, fitted with his heavy-duty triple-chute harness. He was as ready as ever, yet this time he was feeding off her raw energy instead of the other way around. Three hundred feet into Cynthia’s blistering descent her chute tugged open, slowing her to a gentle fall. She unshouldered her rocket launcher as the faint night breeze tousled her hair. Affixing her launcher’s scope, she quickly magnified the Orgoth warlord and her father far below. She gasped at what she saw. Her dread had not been misplaced. Caine was on the ground, motionless on his back, arms and legs spread. He was bloodied and disarmed. Worse, there was a luminous shape emerging from his chest, a brilliant beacon in the night. Oriax stood some five yards away, legs planted wide, arms extended forward as though he were pulling on the light with an invisible cord. She knew it was her father’s soul she was seeing. That familiar scent was already in her nose, and the appetite that ever accompanied it rose in the back of her mind.

name: Name
body:
Her slowed descent had abruptly become torture and for good reason. Her father would be gone before she could land. Where were the Hellslingers? How could things have gone so wrong? As she panned her scope beyond Oriax, answers followed, all of them bad.
There had been a battle here; that much was clear. The supply depot was a burning ruin now—ammunition stores detonated, pockmarked with craters, collapsed tents, and an abandoned front gate. Closest to her father, she spotted Deuce, his dual cannon weapon aimed to strike Oriax from a few yards away. But on closer inspection, she realized her father’s warjack was actually frozen in place. His voltaic cores were ruined; a great hole had been blasted through them, and they still crackled and smoked.
On the other side of Caine, Watts and Ryan lay still on the ground. She could not tell from this distance if they were dead or not. Glover and Falk were nowhere to be found. And rampaging siege tarasks at the depot’s periphery seemed to be in pursuit of something she could not see.

name: Name
body:
She swallowed. It had would have to be her. She readied her weapon and summoned her Gift. Through the void of shadows she slipped, leaving her chute behind, as she had first tried to reach the Tague Bridge. She reappeared a dozen yards down, not quite at terminal velocity but certainly beginning to acquire speed. She wasted no time, pressing her focus to open another shadow, gaining another dozen yards straight down on the other side. Her speed increased though not yet past the point of no return. It did not matter either way. Her father would be gone if she did not.
Another shadow, another leap down, and Cynthia had range. Oriax either did not see her coming or did not care. He had nearly pulled Caine’s soul free of his body, and the scent of it was insufferable to her, filling her nostrils. Anger rose in her. Then Oriax was in her crosshairs, and she fired. She had time enough to see it streaking for him and burst into an indigo fireball as it ruptured his power field instantly. Then she opened one more shadow.

name: Name
body:
On the other side of Cynthia’s portal, Oriax’s visored face broke her fall. Her extended boot would have taken his jaw off but for his mask. Just the same, her speed was such now that the kick struck him like a wrecking ball, knocking him down and taking his helmet from his head in the process. For her part, Cynthia tumbled into a somersault and threw her weapon to the ground. There would be no time now to reload.
Oriax was down, but he was not out. Emboldened by his conquest of Caine, he rose quickly. Powerful hex bolts leapt from his hands straight for her. Blistering pain surged over her, withering her own power field away as she struggled back to her feet. The Orgoth warlord was also not finished with her father. As Caine’s soul sank back into his inert body, Oriax reached forth across the clearing and pulled again, jerking Caine’s luminous form back out of him.
"No." Cynthia fought to shake the spell off even as it sizzled the very air before her. She saw Oriax attempt to retake his prize, and she recognized there was only one play remaining. With both hands, she reached for her father’s soul and unleashed the appetite welling within her.

name: Name
body:
Oriax redoubled his grip on her father with coruscating waves of arcane current, his bare face gaunt and contorted with a desperate, mad grin. Caine whitened even as Oriax regained his footing, now raising both hands to the task. Caine’s soul was pulled forth entirely, his spectral likeness almost fully divorced from his body. As it came free, Oriax celebrated with a howling laugh.
"You can’t have him!" Cynthia braced her footing. She saw large forms around them now, emerging from the shadows of the depot: five siege tarasks as Oriax’s retinue. But it did not matter. There was only Oriax in this moment. As she felt her father’s raw essence emerge fully, that power so long ago formed by Deneghra bloomed inside her.
Oriax laughed, and he bellowed an Orgoth curse, a wild leering look on his face, lit by the power arcing from his fingertips.
Cynthia did not need to speak his language to know he thought he was winning. Her fury was building, growing stronger the more she felt Caine’s soul in her own grasp. It was madness, but she needed it now.

name: Name
body: "I SAID, LET HIM GO." Cynthia spoke with a low voice that was not her own. Black tentacles of purest shadow suddenly spilled out around her. As one, they curled and coiled in a hypnotic display then lunged with blinding speed ahead. The tentacles seized on Caine’s spectral figure, curling first around his legs then snaking up to his chest as Oriax tried to pull him close. Yet Cynthia’s appetite had been unleashed now, and she would not be denied. A tug of war began between the pair. Caine’s soul stretched and warped in the battle, moving back and forth in the struggle. As the seconds wore on, strain tested them both. By her youth or by her Gift, Cynthia appeared to gain the upper hand, feeding her intensity. Caine’s soul moved toward her slowly and then more quickly, his spectral face growing hopeful. Oriax growled like a savage beast, clearly impacted by the strain. His grip on Caine was unraveling. Yet even as the siege tarasks began to circle Cynthia, Pokey and her Gravediggers were finally landing. All opened fire on the way in and wasted no time targeting the riderless beasts, sending them into disarray that Oriax was far too spent to manage. As the tables turned with the arrival of reinforcements, Oriax appeared to panic, uncertain where to fall back. A firefight had begun, and he found himself in the middle of it.

name: Name
body:
He snarled what sounded like a concession. As the nearest tarask stomped past him, he reached out for the creature’s tusk. With the handhold, he swiftly hoisted himself up into the riderless saddle, relinquishing his grip on Caine’s soul altogether. His retinue followed after him, chased at every step by the gunfire from Cynthia’s Gravediggers. Then, as Oriax retreated, a cheer went up among them.
Caine was saved.
Cynthia lowered her guard at last, racing to her father’s inert body lying prone on the ground.
"Are yeh all right, Pa?" She propped him up, took him in her arms. "Pa, wake up!"
Sergeant Baxter was at her side, his face filled with concern. "We found Watts and Ryan across the way."
Cynthia looked up from her unresponsive father. "Are they all right?"
"Trampled both," Baxter explained, "but alive. No sign of Falk or Glover."
"Spread out. Find them." Cynthia held her father.
"Oh, we’re all right." From the wreckage of a pile of ruined crates, Falk reached a hand out. "Could use a bit of help getting out of this mess, though."

name: Name
body:
At Falk’s voice, Caine’s eyes fluttered open.
"Wh…How did yeh?" He looked around, puzzled. "How did yeh get here, kid?"
"I’ll tell yeh all about it." Cynthia grinned, recalling her father’s words all those years ago. "Unless maybe yeh want to get out of here first?"
"More than anything," Caine chuckled.

name: Name
title: Five Fingers, Mabel Bailoch’s Residence\nTen Years Ago

name: Name
body:
"Then Pa here blinks us all back to the skyship, and the evil witch fell to her death!" Cynthia made a dramatic hand gesture for effect and laughed. Next, she finished her cocoa by slamming the mug down, wiping her mouth on her sleeve.
"A lovely story, dear." Mabel Bailoch, the softspoken and elder mother of Kell, chuckled and sat back with a faint smile, looking over the kitchen table between Cynthia and a bandaged Allister Caine, the latter fairly slumped in his chair. "Is any of it true?"
"It’s all true, Ma’am." Cynthia smiled. "Kell made me promise to tell yeh every word, and so I have."
"Such an imagination." Mabel turned to Caine. "Can I get you something, Allister?"
"Another uiske would suit me, Ma’am." He shifted in his seat with a groan, inflaming old wounds.
"Of course." Mabel poured, then glanced at Cynthia over the rim of her spectacles. "Another biscuit, dear?
"Much obliged." Caine reached for his glass with a faint grimace while Cynthia grabbed two more biscuits from the offered plate, stuffing both in her mouth without hesitation.

name: Name
body:
"Well, you certainly look the part." Mabel sipped her tea. "If even half of what you say is true, you really should have taken some rest before coming all this way on my account."
"No time." Caine sighed. "Bossman means to keep me busy from here on out. I’m in trouble enough as it is with this little side caper."
"I appreciate it." Mabel said. "Truth be told, I have no idea what I’m going to do with myself now."
"I reckon yeh’ve some time to figure it out."
It was a story that seemed too good to be true. At the heart of it, she thought of Kell. Though it ofttimes pained her to think upon him, Mabel knew her son well. She knew some of the horrible things he had done in life and could easily imagine there was worse. But to travel to Skell to rescue this little girl? Could he really have done that?
Mabel sipped her tea and reflected.
What was indisputable was this: Allister and Cynthia had arrived overnight, and by morning, Mabel’s master was dead by Allister’s hand, along with every last one of his thugs who didn’t have the sense to run. She was free for the first time in years. The very idea of it yet loomed over her, almost as terrifying as perpetual servitude.

name: Name
body:
Almost.
For so long, any notion of her freedom had been tossed by the wayside for the sake of pragmatic survival. The world was the world. That being the case, the idea that this complete stranger should come all this way and release her from her debt on a whim was patently absurd. In the end, wherever the truth lay, it did not matter. She was free. If this young lady said she was a dragon, that was fine by her.
"So what’s next for you?" Mabel turned back to Cynthia, watching as crumbs spilled from the girl’s overstuffed mouth.
"School." Allister looked over with a stern eye.
"Battle school." Cynthia’s eyes were alight, crumbs spilling. "Caspia."
"Oh, not that again," Allister warned. "I thought I made myself clear. No daughter of mine is going to war."
"But I can fight, Pa." Cynthia scowled. "I have the Gift. No other kid is going through what I did if I could stop it."
"Cynthia," Allister warned then grimaced as his wounds flared.
Mabel saw the look in the girl’s eye; she’d seen it before with her own son. This Allister had no idea what he was up against, but he would find out soon enough.

name: Name
body:
After they’d eaten and finished their drinks, she saw them to the door. As he limped beyond the threshold of her worn domicile, Allister paused and turned.
"I reckon I’m grateful to yer son, Ma’am," he said, watching as Cynthia skipped ahead. "Kell may not have been a good man all the time, but she wouldn’t be here without him."
Mabel was struck by the words. Without warning, a single tear traced its way down her cheek. "Why, thank you, Allister."
Then Cynthia stopped up ahead and turned around.
"I almost forgot," she said, digging into a pocket.
"What is it?" Mabel asked.
"This." Cynthia ran back and pressed a black key into her hand.
"What is it?" Mabel regarded the trinket.
"The key to my cell." Cynthia smiled. "I pinched it off that nasty witch to escape."
"Of course it is. Yes, thank you, Cynthia." Mabel sniffed, putting the key in her pocket.
Then they were gone, down the crowded street and out of her life. She took a minute, thinking about what to do with the rest of the day. As she walked on to the bakery for her daily bread, it was her neighbor Donold who first saw it.

name: Name
body:
"My stars," Donold said, setting his wheelbarrow of dung down to simply stop and stare. He was looking at something overhead, just west of the town gates. Before long, others saw it too, with gasps of amazement fast moving through the street.
Mabel looked up and saw above a ship sailing the sky as easily as if it were in smooth waters. It took her breath away for a moment. A skyship, just as the girl had described it.
"My stars, indeed." Mabel took Cynthia’s key from her pocket and looked it over with newfound wonder.
END

name: Wrath of Caine Part 3 - Chapter 1 The Wrath of Caine:\nPart 3
